/***************************************************************************************************
SECTION 15.3 — BASELINE-RELATIVE FRONTIER DELTAS
****************************************************************************************************

PURPOSE:
    Calculate baseline-relative deltas for each archived strategy slice where a baseline strategy
    exists for the same Module 1 scenario / population / strategy set.

BUSINESS PURPOSE:
    Make frontier interpretation sharper by anchoring each non-baseline strategy point to a
    consistent baseline reference.

    This section answers:

        "Relative to BASELINE_STRATEGY on the same Module 1 scenario and population, what changed in
         access, exposure, approved Expected Loss, affordability, offered-population synthetic risk,
         and reason-code distribution?"

BASELINE DEFINITION:
    The baseline reference is identified by:

        strategy_name = 'BASELINE_STRATEGY'

    within the same:
        strategy_set_name
        module1_scenario_set_name
        module1_scenario_name
        population_id

WHY THIS MATTERS:
    Frontier analysis is more interpretable when strategy points are compared against a consistent
    baseline reference.

    It helps distinguish:
        absolute strategy posture,
        versus baseline-relative movement.

BASELINE UNAVAILABLE BOUNDARY:
    If no baseline strategy exists for a scenario / strategy set, baseline-relative fields are NULL
    and baseline_available_flag is FALSE.

    This is diagnostic behavior, not a failure.

REASON-CODE DELTA DRIVER:
    top_reason_code_delta_driver_* fields identify the simulated reason code with the largest
    population-share movement versus baseline.

    This helps explain not only what changed numerically, but why the strategy frontier point moved.

READ-ONLY BOUNDARY:
    This section reads from archive-derived temporary tables and archive reason-code counts only.

    It does not mutate archive rows.
    It does not recalculate applicant outcomes.
    It does not reassign reason codes.

***************************************************************************************************/

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS tmp_m2_strategy_frontier_baseline_deltas;

CREATE TEMP TABLE tmp_m2_strategy_frontier_baseline_deltas
ON COMMIT PRESERVE ROWS
AS
WITH baseline_reference AS (
    SELECT *
    FROM tmp_m2_strategy_frontier_summary
    WHERE strategy_name = 'BASELINE_STRATEGY'
),

reason_population_shares AS (
    SELECT
        strategy_set_name,
        strategy_name,
        strategy_version,

        module1_scenario_set_name,
        module1_scenario_name,
        population_id,

        primary_reason_family,
        primary_reason_code,

        COUNT(*)::NUMERIC
            / NULLIF(
                SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (
                    PARTITION BY
                        strategy_set_name,
                        strategy_name,
                        strategy_version,
                        module1_scenario_set_name,
                        module1_scenario_name,
                        population_id
                ),
                0
            ) AS reason_population_share

    FROM credit_decisioning_sim.strategy_decisions_archive

    GROUP BY
        strategy_set_name,
        strategy_name,
        strategy_version,
        module1_scenario_set_name,
        module1_scenario_name,
        population_id,
        primary_reason_family,
        primary_reason_code
),

frontier_group_reason_universe AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        strategy_set_name,
        module1_scenario_set_name,
        module1_scenario_name,
        population_id,
        primary_reason_family,
        primary_reason_code
    FROM reason_population_shares
),

baseline_reason_population_shares AS (
    SELECT
        strategy_set_name,
        module1_scenario_set_name,
        module1_scenario_name,
        population_id,
        primary_reason_family,
        primary_reason_code,
        reason_population_share AS baseline_reason_population_share
    FROM reason_population_shares
    WHERE strategy_name = 'BASELINE_STRATEGY'
),

top_reason_code_delta_driver AS (
    SELECT
        s.strategy_set_name,
        s.strategy_name,
        s.strategy_version,
        s.module1_scenario_set_name,
        s.module1_scenario_name,
        s.population_id,

        u.primary_reason_family AS top_reason_code_delta_driver_family,
        u.primary_reason_code AS top_reason_code_delta_driver_code,

        COALESCE(br.baseline_reason_population_share, 0)
            AS top_reason_code_delta_driver_baseline_share,

        COALESCE(rs.reason_population_share, 0)
            AS top_reason_code_delta_driver_strategy_share,

        COALESCE(rs.reason_population_share, 0)
          - COALESCE(br.baseline_reason_population_share, 0)
            AS top_reason_code_delta_population_share,

        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY
                s.strategy_set_name,
                s.strategy_name,
                s.strategy_version,
                s.module1_scenario_set_name,
                s.module1_scenario_name,
                s.population_id
            ORDER BY
                ABS(
                    COALESCE(rs.reason_population_share, 0)
                  - COALESCE(br.baseline_reason_population_share, 0)
                ) DESC,
                u.primary_reason_family,
                u.primary_reason_code
        ) AS reason_code_delta_rank

    FROM tmp_m2_strategy_frontier_summary s

    JOIN frontier_group_reason_universe u
        ON u.strategy_set_name = s.strategy_set_name
       AND u.module1_scenario_set_name = s.module1_scenario_set_name
       AND u.module1_scenario_name = s.module1_scenario_name
       AND u.population_id = s.population_id

    LEFT JOIN reason_population_shares rs
        ON rs.strategy_set_name = s.strategy_set_name
       AND rs.strategy_name = s.strategy_name
       AND rs.strategy_version = s.strategy_version
       AND rs.module1_scenario_set_name = s.module1_scenario_set_name
       AND rs.module1_scenario_name = s.module1_scenario_name
       AND rs.population_id = s.population_id
       AND rs.primary_reason_family = u.primary_reason_family
       AND rs.primary_reason_code = u.primary_reason_code

    LEFT JOIN baseline_reason_population_shares br
        ON br.strategy_set_name = s.strategy_set_name
       AND br.module1_scenario_set_name = s.module1_scenario_set_name
       AND br.module1_scenario_name = s.module1_scenario_name
       AND br.population_id = s.population_id
       AND br.primary_reason_family = u.primary_reason_family
       AND br.primary_reason_code = u.primary_reason_code

    WHERE s.strategy_name <> 'BASELINE_STRATEGY'
)

SELECT
    s.strategy_set_name,
    s.strategy_name,
    s.strategy_version,

    s.module1_scenario_set_name,
    s.module1_scenario_name,
    s.population_id,

    b.strategy_name AS baseline_strategy_name,
    b.strategy_version AS baseline_strategy_version,

    (b.strategy_name IS NOT NULL) AS baseline_available_flag,

    s.applications,
    b.applications AS baseline_applications,
    s.applications - b.applications AS delta_applications,

    s.approval_rate,
    b.approval_rate AS baseline_approval_rate,
    s.approval_rate - b.approval_rate AS delta_approval_rate,

    s.counteroffer_rate,
    b.counteroffer_rate AS baseline_counteroffer_rate,
    s.counteroffer_rate - b.counteroffer_rate AS delta_counteroffer_rate,

    s.manual_review_rate,
    b.manual_review_rate AS baseline_manual_review_rate,
    s.manual_review_rate - b.manual_review_rate AS delta_manual_review_rate,

    s.decline_rate,
    b.decline_rate AS baseline_decline_rate,
    s.decline_rate - b.decline_rate AS delta_decline_rate,

    s.simulated_offer_exposure_rate,
    b.simulated_offer_exposure_rate AS baseline_simulated_offer_exposure_rate,
    s.simulated_offer_exposure_rate - b.simulated_offer_exposure_rate
        AS delta_simulated_offer_exposure_rate,

    s.counteroffer_share_of_offers,
    b.counteroffer_share_of_offers AS baseline_counteroffer_share_of_offers,
    s.counteroffer_share_of_offers - b.counteroffer_share_of_offers
        AS delta_counteroffer_share_of_offers,

    s.total_approved_amount,
    b.total_approved_amount AS baseline_total_approved_amount,
    s.total_approved_amount - b.total_approved_amount AS delta_total_approved_amount,

    s.avg_approved_amount_all_apps,
    b.avg_approved_amount_all_apps AS baseline_avg_approved_amount_all_apps,
    s.avg_approved_amount_all_apps - b.avg_approved_amount_all_apps
        AS delta_avg_approved_amount_all_apps,

    s.avg_approved_amount_offer_rows,
    b.avg_approved_amount_offer_rows AS baseline_avg_approved_amount_offer_rows,
    s.avg_approved_amount_offer_rows - b.avg_approved_amount_offer_rows
        AS delta_avg_approved_amount_offer_rows,

    s.avg_synthetic_estimated_pd_proxy_offer_rows,
    b.avg_synthetic_estimated_pd_proxy_offer_rows
        AS baseline_avg_synthetic_estimated_pd_proxy_offer_rows,
    s.avg_synthetic_estimated_pd_proxy_offer_rows
      - b.avg_synthetic_estimated_pd_proxy_offer_rows
        AS delta_avg_synthetic_estimated_pd_proxy_offer_rows,

    s.avg_approved_payment_to_income_ratio_offer_rows,
    b.avg_approved_payment_to_income_ratio_offer_rows
        AS baseline_avg_approved_payment_to_income_ratio_offer_rows,
    s.avg_approved_payment_to_income_ratio_offer_rows
      - b.avg_approved_payment_to_income_ratio_offer_rows
        AS delta_avg_approved_payment_to_income_ratio_offer_rows,

    s.total_requested_expected_loss_amount,
    b.total_requested_expected_loss_amount AS baseline_total_requested_expected_loss_amount,
    s.total_requested_expected_loss_amount - b.total_requested_expected_loss_amount
        AS delta_total_requested_expected_loss_amount,

    s.total_approved_expected_loss_amount,
    b.total_approved_expected_loss_amount AS baseline_total_approved_expected_loss_amount,
    s.total_approved_expected_loss_amount - b.total_approved_expected_loss_amount
        AS delta_total_approved_expected_loss_amount,

    s.avg_approved_expected_loss_offer_rows,
    b.avg_approved_expected_loss_offer_rows
        AS baseline_avg_approved_expected_loss_offer_rows,
    s.avg_approved_expected_loss_offer_rows
      - b.avg_approved_expected_loss_offer_rows
        AS delta_avg_approved_expected_loss_offer_rows,

    s.approved_expected_loss_rate,
    b.approved_expected_loss_rate AS baseline_approved_expected_loss_rate,
    s.approved_expected_loss_rate - b.approved_expected_loss_rate
        AS delta_approved_expected_loss_rate,

    s.top_primary_reason_family,
    s.top_primary_reason_code,
    s.top_primary_reason_population_share,

    s.top_non_approval_primary_reason_family,
    s.top_non_approval_primary_reason_code,
    s.top_non_approval_reason_population_share,

    s.top_policy_stop_primary_reason_family,
    s.top_policy_stop_primary_reason_code,
    s.top_policy_stop_reason_population_share,

    td.top_reason_code_delta_driver_family,
    td.top_reason_code_delta_driver_code,
    td.top_reason_code_delta_driver_baseline_share,
    td.top_reason_code_delta_driver_strategy_share,
    td.top_reason_code_delta_population_share

FROM tmp_m2_strategy_frontier_summary s

LEFT JOIN baseline_reference b
    ON b.strategy_set_name = s.strategy_set_name
   AND b.module1_scenario_set_name = s.module1_scenario_set_name
   AND b.module1_scenario_name = s.module1_scenario_name
   AND b.population_id = s.population_id

LEFT JOIN top_reason_code_delta_driver td
    ON td.strategy_set_name = s.strategy_set_name
   AND td.strategy_name = s.strategy_name
   AND td.strategy_version = s.strategy_version
   AND td.module1_scenario_set_name = s.module1_scenario_set_name
   AND td.module1_scenario_name = s.module1_scenario_name
   AND td.population_id = s.population_id
   AND td.reason_code_delta_rank = 1;

/***************************************************************************************************
SECTION 15.4 — STRATEGY EFFICIENCY METRICS
****************************************************************************************************

PURPOSE:
    Convert frontier summary metrics into executive-readable efficiency indicators.

BUSINESS PURPOSE:
    Support strategy posture comparison by translating raw frontier metrics into compact efficiency
    signals.

    This section answers:

        "How much simulated approved exposure, simulated offer access, and portfolio coverage is
         produced relative to approved Expected Loss?"

SQL PURPOSE:
    1. Materialize tmp_m2_strategy_frontier_efficiency.
    2. Calculate frontier_approved_expected_loss_rate.
    3. Calculate approved_amount_per_approved_expected_loss_dollar.
    4. Calculate offer_rate_per_approved_expected_loss_rate_unit.
    5. Calculate applications_per_million_approved_expected_loss.
    6. Carry positive_offer_access_rate.
    7. Carry manual_review_burden_rate.
    8. Carry no_offer_outcome_rate.
    9. Assign frontier_efficiency_metric_status.

BUSINESS INTERPRETATION:
    These metrics help compare strategy posture.

    Examples:
        How much approved exposure is produced per unit of approved Expected Loss?
        How many simulated positive offer outcomes are produced per million dollars of approved
        Expected Loss?
        What is the approved Expected Loss rate on simulated approved exposure?
        How much manual-review burden does the strategy create?
        What share of the population receives simulated positive offer exposure?

IMPORTANT:
    These are comparative synthetic strategy metrics.

    They are not:
        profitability,
        capital,
        pricing,
        funding cost,
        margin,
        account performance,
        or production risk-adjusted return metrics.

    Those are intentionally deferred to future Module 3.

BOUNDARY:
    Efficiency metrics are calculated from already archived outputs.

    Section 15.4 does not recalculate approved amount or approved Expected Loss.

***************************************************************************************************/

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS tmp_m2_strategy_frontier_efficiency;

CREATE TEMP TABLE tmp_m2_strategy_frontier_efficiency
ON COMMIT PRESERVE ROWS
AS
SELECT
    d.*,

    d.total_approved_expected_loss_amount
        / NULLIF(d.total_approved_amount, 0)
        AS frontier_approved_expected_loss_rate,

    d.total_approved_amount
        / NULLIF(d.total_approved_expected_loss_amount, 0)
        AS approved_amount_per_approved_expected_loss_dollar,

    d.simulated_offer_exposure_rate
        / NULLIF(d.approved_expected_loss_rate, 0)
        AS offer_rate_per_approved_expected_loss_rate_unit,

    d.applications::NUMERIC
        / NULLIF(d.total_approved_expected_loss_amount / 1000000.0, 0)
        AS applications_per_million_approved_expected_loss,

    d.simulated_offer_exposure_rate AS positive_offer_access_rate,

    d.manual_review_rate AS manual_review_burden_rate,

    d.decline_rate AS no_offer_outcome_rate,

    CASE
        WHEN d.total_approved_amount IS NULL
          OR d.total_approved_amount = 0
            THEN 'NO_SIMULATED_OFFER_EXPOSURE_FOR_EFFICIENCY_REVIEW'

        WHEN d.total_approved_expected_loss_amount IS NULL
            THEN 'APPROVED_EXPECTED_LOSS_NOT_AVAILABLE_FOR_EFFICIENCY_REVIEW'

        ELSE 'FRONTIER_EFFICIENCY_METRICS_AVAILABLE'
    END AS frontier_efficiency_metric_status

FROM tmp_m2_strategy_frontier_baseline_deltas d;

/***************************************************************************************************
SECTION 15.5 — FRONTIER CLASSIFICATION
****************************************************************************************************

PURPOSE:
    Assign diagnostic strategy posture labels to each archived frontier point.

BUSINESS PURPOSE:
    Translate numeric frontier metrics into readable strategy posture labels that can support
    executive discussion, README interpretation, and LinkedIn storytelling.

    This section answers:

        "What kind of tradeoff does this archived strategy point appear to represent?"

SQL PURPOSE:
    1. Materialize tmp_m2_strategy_frontier_classification.
    2. Preserve efficiency metrics and baseline-relative deltas.
    3. Assign frontier_position_type.
    4. Assign frontier_interpretation_note.
    5. Display classification output with relevant frontier metrics.

FRONTIER POSITION TYPES:
    BASELINE_REFERENCE_POINT:
        Baseline strategy under the same scenario / population / strategy set.

    NO_BASELINE_REFERENCE_AVAILABLE:
        Strategy slice exists but baseline-relative deltas are unavailable.

    RISK_DISCIPLINE_FRONTIER_POINT:
        Strategy reduces simulated offer exposure and approved Expected Loss while improving the
        offered-population synthetic estimated-risk profile.

    GROWTH_ORIENTED_FRONTIER_POINT:
        Strategy expands simulated offer exposure and approved amount with measurable approved
        Expected Loss tradeoff.

    EXPOSURE_EFFICIENT_FRONTIER_POINT:
        Strategy improves approved Expected Loss while maintaining or expanding total approved amount.

    COUNTEROFFER_MANAGEMENT_FRONTIER_POINT:
        Strategy shifts outcomes toward reduced-exposure treatment rather than clean approval.

    REVIEW_BURDEN_REDUCTION_FRONTIER_POINT:
        Strategy reduces unresolved manual-review burden by routing more cases to final no-offer
        outcomes.

    BALANCED_OR_MIXED_FRONTIER_POINT:
        Strategy shows mixed tradeoffs requiring segment-level and reason-code review.

CLASSIFICATION BOUNDARY:
    These labels are diagnostic summaries.

    They do not declare a strategy "best."
    They do not recommend production use.
    They do not replace Section 13 matched comparison.
    They do not replace Section 14 validation.
    They do not represent model validation approval.

DIAGNOSTIC THRESHOLD NOTE:
    Small threshold values are used only to avoid labeling immaterial changes as strategic movement.

    These thresholds are not:
        credit policy thresholds,
        underwriting cutoffs,
        production acceptance thresholds,
        calibrated empirical performance thresholds,
        or regulatory standards.

***************************************************************************************************/

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS tmp_m2_strategy_frontier_classification;

CREATE TEMP TABLE tmp_m2_strategy_frontier_classification
ON COMMIT PRESERVE ROWS
AS
SELECT
    e.*,

    CASE
        WHEN e.strategy_name = 'BASELINE_STRATEGY'
            THEN 'BASELINE_REFERENCE_POINT'

        WHEN e.baseline_available_flag IS DISTINCT FROM TRUE
            THEN 'NO_BASELINE_REFERENCE_AVAILABLE'

        WHEN e.delta_simulated_offer_exposure_rate <= -0.010
         AND e.delta_total_approved_expected_loss_amount < 0
         AND e.delta_avg_synthetic_estimated_pd_proxy_offer_rows < 0
            THEN 'RISK_DISCIPLINE_FRONTIER_POINT'

        WHEN e.delta_simulated_offer_exposure_rate >= 0.010
         AND e.delta_total_approved_amount > 0
         AND e.delta_total_approved_expected_loss_amount >= 0
            THEN 'GROWTH_ORIENTED_FRONTIER_POINT'

        WHEN e.delta_total_approved_expected_loss_amount < 0
         AND e.delta_total_approved_amount >= 0
            THEN 'EXPOSURE_EFFICIENT_FRONTIER_POINT'

        WHEN e.delta_counteroffer_rate >= 0.010
         AND e.delta_approval_rate <= 0
            THEN 'COUNTEROFFER_MANAGEMENT_FRONTIER_POINT'

        WHEN e.delta_manual_review_rate <= -0.010
         AND e.delta_decline_rate > 0
            THEN 'REVIEW_BURDEN_REDUCTION_FRONTIER_POINT'

        ELSE 'BALANCED_OR_MIXED_FRONTIER_POINT'
    END AS frontier_position_type,

    CASE
        WHEN e.strategy_name = 'BASELINE_STRATEGY'
            THEN 'Reference point for same Module 1 scenario / population / strategy set.'

        WHEN e.baseline_available_flag IS DISTINCT FROM TRUE
            THEN 'No baseline strategy slice exists for this Module 1 scenario / population / strategy set.'

        WHEN e.delta_simulated_offer_exposure_rate <= -0.010
         AND e.delta_total_approved_expected_loss_amount < 0
         AND e.delta_avg_synthetic_estimated_pd_proxy_offer_rows < 0
            THEN 'Strategy reduces simulated offer exposure and approved Expected Loss while improving offered-population synthetic estimated-risk profile.'

        WHEN e.delta_simulated_offer_exposure_rate >= 0.010
         AND e.delta_total_approved_amount > 0
         AND e.delta_total_approved_expected_loss_amount >= 0
            THEN 'Strategy expands simulated offer exposure and approved amount with measurable approved Expected Loss tradeoff.'

        WHEN e.delta_total_approved_expected_loss_amount < 0
         AND e.delta_total_approved_amount >= 0
            THEN 'Strategy improves approved Expected Loss while maintaining or expanding total approved amount.'

        WHEN e.delta_counteroffer_rate >= 0.010
         AND e.delta_approval_rate <= 0
            THEN 'Strategy shifts outcomes toward reduced-exposure treatment rather than clean approval.'

        WHEN e.delta_manual_review_rate <= -0.010
         AND e.delta_decline_rate > 0
            THEN 'Strategy reduces unresolved manual-review burden by routing more cases to final no-offer outcomes.'

        ELSE 'Strategy shows mixed tradeoffs requiring segment-level and reason-code review.'
    END AS frontier_interpretation_note

FROM tmp_m2_strategy_frontier_efficiency e;

/***************************************************************************************************
SECTION 15.6 — SEGMENT-LEVEL FRONTIER HIGHLIGHTS
****************************************************************************************************

PURPOSE:
    Provide product, score-band, and product × score-band frontier summaries across archived slices.

BUSINESS PURPOSE:
    Identify where portfolio-level frontier movement is concentrated.

    This section answers:

        "Which products, score bands, and product × score intersections carry the most approved
         exposure, approved Expected Loss, access movement, affordability pressure, or reason-code
         concentration?"

SQL PURPOSE:
    1. Materialize tmp_m2_strategy_frontier_segment_highlights.
    2. Create segment views at three levels:
            PRODUCT
            SCORE_BAND
            PRODUCT_X_SCORE
    3. Summarize applications, decision rates, simulated offer exposure, approved amount, approved
       Expected Loss, approved Expected Loss rate, offered-population synthetic estimated-risk proxy,
       and approved PTI.
    4. Identify the top simulated reason code within each segment.
    5. Display segment highlights, ordered toward higher approved Expected Loss exposure.

BUSINESS INTERPRETATION:
    Portfolio-level frontier metrics can hide concentrated segment movement.

    Segment-level highlights help reviewers answer:
        Which products carry the most approved exposure?
        Which score bands dominate approved Expected Loss?
        Which product × score combinations are most sensitive to strategy posture?
        Which reason codes explain segment concentration?

WHY PRODUCT × SCORE IS INCLUDED:
    Product and score band are two of the most important strategy dimensions.

    Product shapes structure, exposure, payment behavior, LGD, counteroffer feasibility, and product
    guardrails.

    Score band shapes borrower-quality segmentation and synthetic estimated-risk ordering.

    Reviewing them jointly prevents high-level averages from hiding concentrated behavior.

BOUNDARY:
    This is a segment summary over archived outputs.

    It does not recalculate decisions.
    It does not recalculate approved exposure.
    It does not recalculate approved Expected Loss.
    It does not reassign reason codes.
    It does not create a permanent reporting mart.

***************************************************************************************************/

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS tmp_m2_strategy_frontier_segment_highlights;

CREATE TEMP TABLE tmp_m2_strategy_frontier_segment_highlights
ON COMMIT PRESERVE ROWS
AS
WITH segment_base AS (
    SELECT
        'PRODUCT'::TEXT AS segment_level,
        product_type_policy_key AS segment_key,
        product_type_policy_key,
        NULL::TEXT AS score_band_policy_key,

        strategy_set_name,
        strategy_name,
        strategy_version,
        module1_scenario_set_name,
        module1_scenario_name,
        population_id,

        decision_outcome,
        simulated_offer_exposure_flag,
        approved_amount,
        approved_expected_loss_amount,
        estimated_pd,
        approved_payment_to_income_ratio,
        primary_reason_family,
        primary_reason_code

    FROM credit_decisioning_sim.strategy_decisions_archive

    UNION ALL

    SELECT
        'SCORE_BAND'::TEXT AS segment_level,
        score_band_policy_key AS segment_key,
        NULL::TEXT AS product_type_policy_key,
        score_band_policy_key,

        strategy_set_name,
        strategy_name,
        strategy_version,
        module1_scenario_set_name,
        module1_scenario_name,
        population_id,

        decision_outcome,
        simulated_offer_exposure_flag,
        approved_amount,
        approved_expected_loss_amount,
        estimated_pd,
        approved_payment_to_income_ratio,
        primary_reason_family,
        primary_reason_code

    FROM credit_decisioning_sim.strategy_decisions_archive

    UNION ALL

    SELECT
        'PRODUCT_X_SCORE'::TEXT AS segment_level,
        product_type_policy_key || ' / ' || score_band_policy_key AS segment_key,
        product_type_policy_key,
        score_band_policy_key,

        strategy_set_name,
        strategy_name,
        strategy_version,
        module1_scenario_set_name,
        module1_scenario_name,
        population_id,

        decision_outcome,
        simulated_offer_exposure_flag,
        approved_amount,
        approved_expected_loss_amount,
        estimated_pd,
        approved_payment_to_income_ratio,
        primary_reason_family,
        primary_reason_code

    FROM credit_decisioning_sim.strategy_decisions_archive
),

segment_summary AS (
    SELECT
        segment_level,
        segment_key,
        product_type_policy_key,
        score_band_policy_key,

        strategy_set_name,
        strategy_name,
        strategy_version,
        module1_scenario_set_name,
        module1_scenario_name,
        population_id,

        COUNT(*) AS applications,

        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE decision_outcome = 'APPROVE')::NUMERIC
            / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS approval_rate,

        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE decision_outcome = 'COUNTEROFFER')::NUMERIC
            / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS counteroffer_rate,

        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE decision_outcome = 'MANUAL_REVIEW')::NUMERIC
            / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS manual_review_rate,

        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE decision_outcome = 'DECLINE')::NUMERIC
            / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS decline_rate,

        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE simulated_offer_exposure_flag IS TRUE)::NUMERIC
            / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS simulated_offer_exposure_rate,

        SUM(COALESCE(approved_amount, 0)) AS total_approved_amount,

        AVG(approved_amount) FILTER (WHERE simulated_offer_exposure_flag IS TRUE)
            AS avg_approved_amount_offer_rows,

        SUM(COALESCE(approved_expected_loss_amount, 0))
            AS total_approved_expected_loss_amount,

        AVG(approved_expected_loss_amount) FILTER (WHERE simulated_offer_exposure_flag IS TRUE)
            AS avg_approved_expected_loss_offer_rows,

        SUM(COALESCE(approved_expected_loss_amount, 0))
            / NULLIF(SUM(COALESCE(approved_amount, 0)), 0)
            AS approved_expected_loss_rate,

        AVG(estimated_pd) FILTER (WHERE simulated_offer_exposure_flag IS TRUE)
            AS avg_synthetic_estimated_pd_proxy_offer_rows,

        AVG(approved_payment_to_income_ratio) FILTER (WHERE simulated_offer_exposure_flag IS TRUE)
            AS avg_approved_payment_to_income_ratio_offer_rows

    FROM segment_base

    GROUP BY
        segment_level,
        segment_key,
        product_type_policy_key,
        score_band_policy_key,
        strategy_set_name,
        strategy_name,
        strategy_version,
        module1_scenario_set_name,
        module1_scenario_name,
        population_id
),

segment_reason_counts AS (
    SELECT
        segment_level,
        segment_key,
        product_type_policy_key,
        score_band_policy_key,

        strategy_set_name,
        strategy_name,
        strategy_version,
        module1_scenario_set_name,
        module1_scenario_name,
        population_id,

        primary_reason_family,
        primary_reason_code,

        COUNT(*) AS reason_row_count,

        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY
                segment_level,
                segment_key,
                strategy_set_name,
                strategy_name,
                strategy_version,
                module1_scenario_set_name,
                module1_scenario_name,
                population_id
            ORDER BY
                COUNT(*) DESC,
                primary_reason_family,
                primary_reason_code
        ) AS reason_rank

    FROM segment_base

    GROUP BY
        segment_level,
        segment_key,
        product_type_policy_key,
        score_band_policy_key,
        strategy_set_name,
        strategy_name,
        strategy_version,
        module1_scenario_set_name,
        module1_scenario_name,
        population_id,
        primary_reason_family,
        primary_reason_code
)

SELECT
    s.*,

    r.primary_reason_family AS top_segment_reason_family,
    r.primary_reason_code AS top_segment_reason_code,
    r.reason_row_count AS top_segment_reason_row_count

FROM segment_summary s

LEFT JOIN segment_reason_counts r
    ON r.segment_level = s.segment_level
   AND r.segment_key = s.segment_key
   AND r.strategy_set_name = s.strategy_set_name
   AND r.strategy_name = s.strategy_name
   AND r.strategy_version = s.strategy_version
   AND r.module1_scenario_set_name = s.module1_scenario_set_name
   AND r.module1_scenario_name = s.module1_scenario_name
   AND r.population_id = s.population_id
   AND r.reason_rank = 1;


/*-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
15.6A Segment-level frontier highlights review output.

Purpose:
    Display product, score-band, and product × score-band frontier segment summaries.

Interpretation:

    The ORDER BY prioritizes higher approved Expected Loss segments because those are usually the

Boundary:

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------*/

SELECT

LIMIT 300;



/***************************************************************************************************
SECTION 15.7 — EXECUTIVE-READY STRATEGY FRONTIER SUMMARY
****************************************************************************************************

PURPOSE:
    Produce a compact strategy frontier table suitable for export into a README, executive review,
    LinkedIn result summary, future presentation artifact, or Section 16 evidence capture.

BUSINESS PURPOSE:
    Convert the strategy frontier into one table that can tell the executive story of each archived
    strategy / scenario point.

    This section answers:

        "What is the concise executive interpretation of each archived strategy frontier point?"

SQL PURPOSE:
    1. Materialize tmp_m2_strategy_frontier_executive_summary.
    2. Rank strategies within each frontier group by:
            simulated offer exposure,
            total approved amount,
            total approved Expected Loss,
            approved Expected Loss rate,
            offered-population synthetic estimated-risk proxy,
            manual-review burden,
            decline burden.
    3. Carry core frontier metrics.
    4. Carry baseline-relative deltas.
    5. Carry top reason-code fields.
    6. Carry optional campaign registry fields where a registry mapping exists.
    7. Assign executive_frontier_quadrant.

REGISTRY PATCH:
    This section now LEFT JOINs the archived frontier technical key to:

        tmp_m2_strategy_frontier_campaign_registry_map

    and carries:

        frontier_registry_match_status
        frontier_registry_match_count
        module1_run_id
        module2_run_id
        run_sequence_number
        showcase_id
        showcase_name
        comparison_group_id
        validation_evidence_group_id
        readme_storyline_label
        linkedin_post_sequence
        validation_summary_section_hint

    These fields make Section 15 suitable as a standalone frontier export.

REGISTRY INTERPRETATION:
    FRONTIER_REGISTRY_MATCHED:
        The archived frontier row has exactly one active campaign registry mapping.

    FRONTIER_REGISTRY_DUPLICATE_MATCH_REVIEW:
        More than one active registry row exists for the same technical key. Section 15 selected one
        ranked mapping to avoid duplicate frontier rows, but the registry should be reviewed.

    FRONTIER_REGISTRY_NOT_FOUND:
        No active registry row exists for this archived frontier point.

        The frontier metrics remain valid, but documentation linkage is incomplete.

BUSINESS INTERPRETATION:
    This table intentionally combines:
        decision distribution,
        simulated offer exposure,
        approved exposure,
        approved Expected Loss,
        efficiency metrics,
        strategy posture classification,
        reason-code concentration,
        reason-code movement,
        frontier ranks,
        and campaign registry identifiers.

    It is designed to support a concise story:

        "What tradeoff does each strategy / scenario point represent?"

RANKING BOUNDARY:
    Rankings are calculated within each:
        strategy_set_name
        module1_scenario_set_name
        module1_scenario_name
        population_id

    These ranks support comparison.

    They do not declare production suitability.
    They do not identify a single approved strategy.
    They do not replace Section 13 matched comparison or Section 14 validation.

EXECUTIVE FRONTIER QUADRANT BOUNDARY:
    executive_frontier_quadrant is a diagnostic storytelling label.

    It is not a production recommendation.
    It is not a risk appetite approval.
    It is not a validation acceptance decision.

***************************************************************************************************/

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS tmp_m2_strategy_frontier_executive_summary;

CREATE TEMP TABLE tmp_m2_strategy_frontier_executive_summary
ON COMMIT PRESERVE ROWS
AS
WITH ranked AS (
    SELECT
        c.*,

        COUNT(*) OVER (
            PARTITION BY
                strategy_set_name,
                module1_scenario_set_name,
                module1_scenario_name,
                population_id
        ) AS strategy_count_within_frontier_group,

        RANK() OVER (
            PARTITION BY
                strategy_set_name,
                module1_scenario_set_name,
                module1_scenario_name,
                population_id
            ORDER BY
                simulated_offer_exposure_rate DESC NULLS LAST
        ) AS offer_access_rank_desc,

        RANK() OVER (
            PARTITION BY
                strategy_set_name,
                module1_scenario_set_name,
                module1_scenario_name,
                population_id
            ORDER BY
                total_approved_amount DESC NULLS LAST
        ) AS approved_amount_rank_desc,

        RANK() OVER (
            PARTITION BY
                strategy_set_name,
                module1_scenario_set_name,
                module1_scenario_name,
                population_id
            ORDER BY
                total_approved_expected_loss_amount ASC NULLS LAST
        ) AS total_approved_expected_loss_rank_asc,

        RANK() OVER (
            PARTITION BY
                strategy_set_name,
                module1_scenario_set_name,
                module1_scenario_name,
                population_id
            ORDER BY
                approved_expected_loss_rate ASC NULLS LAST
        ) AS approved_expected_loss_rate_rank_asc,

        RANK() OVER (
            PARTITION BY
                strategy_set_name,
                module1_scenario_set_name,
                module1_scenario_name,
                population_id
            ORDER BY
                avg_synthetic_estimated_pd_proxy_offer_rows ASC NULLS LAST
        ) AS offer_risk_profile_rank_asc,

        RANK() OVER (
            PARTITION BY
                strategy_set_name,
                module1_scenario_set_name,
                module1_scenario_name,
                population_id
            ORDER BY
                manual_review_rate ASC NULLS LAST
        ) AS manual_review_burden_rank_asc,

        RANK() OVER (
            PARTITION BY
                strategy_set_name,
                module1_scenario_set_name,
                module1_scenario_name,
                population_id
            ORDER BY
                decline_rate ASC NULLS LAST
        ) AS decline_burden_rank_asc

    FROM tmp_m2_strategy_frontier_classification c
)

SELECT
    /***********************************************************************************************
    Optional campaign registry linkage.

    These fields are documentation and evidence-linkage metadata.

    They do not replace the technical frontier grain.
    ***********************************************************************************************/
    COALESCE(reg.frontier_registry_match_status, 'FRONTIER_REGISTRY_NOT_FOUND')
        AS frontier_registry_match_status,

    COALESCE(reg.registry_match_count, 0)
        AS frontier_registry_match_count,

    reg.module1_run_id,
    reg.module2_run_id,
    reg.run_sequence_number,

    reg.showcase_id,
    reg.showcase_name,
    reg.comparison_group_id,
    reg.validation_evidence_group_id,

    reg.readme_storyline_label,
    reg.linkedin_post_sequence,
    reg.validation_summary_section_hint,

    /***********************************************************************************************
    Technical Module 1 scenario / population grain.
    ***********************************************************************************************/
    r.module1_scenario_set_name,
    r.module1_scenario_name,
    r.population_id,

    /***********************************************************************************************
    Technical Module 2 strategy grain.
    ***********************************************************************************************/
    r.strategy_set_name,
    r.strategy_name,
    r.strategy_version,

    /***********************************************************************************************
    Frontier posture labels.
    ***********************************************************************************************/
    r.frontier_position_type,
    r.frontier_interpretation_note,

    r.strategy_count_within_frontier_group,

    r.applications,

    r.approval_rate,
    r.counteroffer_rate,
    r.manual_review_rate,
    r.decline_rate,
    r.simulated_offer_exposure_rate,
    r.counteroffer_share_of_offers,

    r.total_approved_amount,
    r.avg_approved_amount_offer_rows,

    r.avg_synthetic_estimated_pd_proxy_offer_rows,
    r.avg_approved_payment_to_income_ratio_offer_rows,

    r.total_approved_expected_loss_amount,
    r.avg_approved_expected_loss_offer_rows,
    r.approved_expected_loss_rate,

    r.approved_amount_per_approved_expected_loss_dollar,

    r.top_primary_reason_family,
    r.top_primary_reason_code,
    r.top_primary_reason_population_share,

    r.top_non_approval_primary_reason_family,
    r.top_non_approval_primary_reason_code,
    r.top_non_approval_reason_population_share,

    r.top_policy_stop_primary_reason_family,
    r.top_policy_stop_primary_reason_code,
    r.top_policy_stop_reason_population_share,

    r.top_reason_code_delta_driver_family,
    r.top_reason_code_delta_driver_code,
    r.top_reason_code_delta_driver_baseline_share,
    r.top_reason_code_delta_driver_strategy_share,
    r.top_reason_code_delta_population_share,

    r.baseline_available_flag,

    r.delta_approval_rate,
    r.delta_counteroffer_rate,
    r.delta_manual_review_rate,
    r.delta_decline_rate,
    r.delta_simulated_offer_exposure_rate,

    r.delta_total_approved_amount,
    r.delta_total_approved_expected_loss_amount,
    r.delta_approved_expected_loss_rate,
    r.delta_avg_synthetic_estimated_pd_proxy_offer_rows,

    r.offer_access_rank_desc,
    r.approved_amount_rank_desc,
    r.total_approved_expected_loss_rank_asc,
    r.approved_expected_loss_rate_rank_asc,
    r.offer_risk_profile_rank_asc,
    r.manual_review_burden_rank_asc,
    r.decline_burden_rank_asc,

    CASE
        WHEN r.strategy_name = 'BASELINE_STRATEGY'
            THEN 'BASELINE_REFERENCE_QUADRANT'

        WHEN r.strategy_count_within_frontier_group < 3
         AND r.delta_simulated_offer_exposure_rate < 0
         AND r.delta_approved_expected_loss_rate < 0
            THEN 'LOWER_ACCESS_LOWER_APPROVED_EL_RATE'

        WHEN r.strategy_count_within_frontier_group < 3
         AND r.delta_simulated_offer_exposure_rate > 0
         AND r.delta_approved_expected_loss_rate > 0
            THEN 'HIGHER_ACCESS_HIGHER_APPROVED_EL_RATE'

        WHEN r.strategy_count_within_frontier_group < 3
         AND r.delta_simulated_offer_exposure_rate >= 0
         AND r.delta_approved_expected_loss_rate <= 0
            THEN 'HIGHER_ACCESS_LOWER_APPROVED_EL_RATE'

        WHEN r.strategy_count_within_frontier_group < 3
         AND r.delta_simulated_offer_exposure_rate <= 0
         AND r.delta_approved_expected_loss_rate >= 0
            THEN 'LOWER_ACCESS_HIGHER_APPROVED_EL_RATE'

        WHEN r.strategy_count_within_frontier_group < 3
            THEN 'TWO_STRATEGY_MIXED_FRONTIER_REVIEW'

        WHEN r.offer_access_rank_desc <= 2
         AND r.approved_expected_loss_rate_rank_asc <= 2
            THEN 'HIGH_ACCESS_LOWER_APPROVED_EL_RATE'

        WHEN r.offer_access_rank_desc <= 2
         AND r.approved_expected_loss_rate_rank_asc > 2
            THEN 'HIGH_ACCESS_HIGHER_APPROVED_EL_RATE'

        WHEN r.offer_access_rank_desc > 2
         AND r.approved_expected_loss_rate_rank_asc <= 2
            THEN 'LOWER_ACCESS_LOWER_APPROVED_EL_RATE'

        ELSE 'LOWER_ACCESS_HIGHER_APPROVED_EL_RATE'
    END AS executive_frontier_quadrant

FROM ranked r

LEFT JOIN tmp_m2_strategy_frontier_campaign_registry_map reg
    ON reg.strategy_set_name = r.strategy_set_name
   AND reg.strategy_name = r.strategy_name
   AND reg.strategy_version = r.strategy_version
   AND reg.module1_scenario_set_name = r.module1_scenario_set_name
   AND reg.module1_scenario_name = r.module1_scenario_name
   AND reg.population_id = r.population_id;


/*-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
15.7A Executive-ready strategy frontier summary review output.

Purpose:
    Display the primary Section 15 output for high-level strategy storytelling.

Interpretation:
    This is the table most likely to be exported later for:
        README summaries,
        LinkedIn posts,
        executive review,
        validation-summary support,
        and strategy campaign evidence.

Registry interpretation:
    Rows with FRONTIER_REGISTRY_MATCHED are directly linked to the formal campaign registry.

    Rows with FRONTIER_REGISTRY_NOT_FOUND are still valid frontier rows, but they do not yet have
    formal campaign IDs attached.

Boundary:

    strategy_version;

/***************************************************************************************************
SECTION 15.8B — FRONTIER BASELINE AVAILABILITY DIAGNOSTIC
****************************************************************************************************

PURPOSE:
    Confirm whether archived frontier rows have baseline references available.

BUSINESS INTERPRETATION:
    Baseline-relative deltas are most useful when every strategy frontier row has a matching
    BASELINE_STRATEGY under the same Module 1 scenario / population / strategy set.

INTERPRETATION:
    If baseline_available_flag is FALSE, baseline-relative deltas for that archived strategy /
    scenario slice should be interpreted as unavailable rather than zero.

STATUS VALUES:
    BASELINE_REFERENCES_AVAILABLE_FOR_ALL_FRONTIER_ROWS:
        All frontier rows in the group have baseline references.

    BASELINE_REFERENCE_MISSING_FOR_ONE_OR_MORE_FRONTIER_ROWS:
        At least one frontier row lacks a baseline reference.

BOUNDARY:
    Missing baseline reference is not an archive failure by itself.

    It is a comparison-readiness and storytelling limitation.

***************************************************************************************************/

SELECT
    strategy_set_name,
    module1_scenario_set_name,
    module1_scenario_name,
    population_id,

    COUNT(*) AS frontier_rows,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE baseline_available_flag IS TRUE) AS rows_with_baseline_reference,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE baseline_available_flag IS FALSE) AS rows_without_baseline_reference,

    CASE
        WHEN COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE baseline_available_flag IS FALSE) = 0
            THEN 'BASELINE_REFERENCES_AVAILABLE_FOR_ALL_FRONTIER_ROWS'
        ELSE 'BASELINE_REFERENCE_MISSING_FOR_ONE_OR_MORE_FRONTIER_ROWS'
    END AS baseline_reference_status

FROM tmp_m2_strategy_frontier_baseline_deltas

GROUP BY
    strategy_set_name,
    module1_scenario_set_name,
    module1_scenario_name,
    population_id

ORDER BY
    strategy_set_name,
    module1_scenario_set_name,
    module1_scenario_name,
    population_id;



/***************************************************************************************************
SECTION 15.8C — FRONTIER REASON-CODE STORYTELLING DIAGNOSTIC
****************************************************************************************************

PURPOSE:
    Provide a compact reason-code interpretation view for the strategy frontier summary.

BUSINESS PURPOSE:
    Help explain each archived strategy frontier point by highlighting:
        the top primary reason code overall,
        the top non-approval reason code,
        the top policy-stop reason code,
        and the reason code with the largest population-share movement versus baseline.

BUSINESS INTERPRETATION:
    This diagnostic helps explain not just how the frontier moved, but why.

    It is especially useful because:
        top_primary_reason_code is often APPROVED_AS_REQUESTED,
        which is technically correct but not always the most useful explanation of strategy movement.

    The non-approval and policy-stop fields provide better visibility into risk tightening,
    affordability constraints, exposure constraints, counteroffer management, or no-offer drivers.

REGISTRY PATCH:
    This output includes module2_run_id, showcase_id, comparison_group_id, and
    validation_evidence_group_id where available so the reason-code story can be copied directly into
    campaign documentation.

BOUNDARY:
    This is a read-only storytelling diagnostic.

    It does not recalculate decision outcomes.
    It does not reassign simulated reason codes.
    It does not modify latest-run rows.
    It does not modify archive rows.
    Reason codes remain simulated strategy explanation codes only.

***************************************************************************************************/

SELECT
    frontier_registry_match_status,
    module1_run_id,
    module2_run_id,
    run_sequence_number,
    showcase_id,
    showcase_name,
    comparison_group_id,
    validation_evidence_group_id,

    strategy_name,
    frontier_position_type,
    executive_frontier_quadrant,

    top_primary_reason_code,
    top_primary_reason_population_share,

    top_non_approval_primary_reason_code,
    top_non_approval_reason_population_share,

    top_policy_stop_primary_reason_code,
    top_policy_stop_reason_population_share,

    top_reason_code_delta_driver_code,
    top_reason_code_delta_driver_baseline_share,
    top_reason_code_delta_driver_strategy_share,
    top_reason_code_delta_population_share

FROM tmp_m2_strategy_frontier_executive_summary

ORDER BY
    module1_scenario_set_name,
    module1_scenario_name,
    population_id,
    strategy_set_name,
    CASE
        WHEN strategy_name = 'BASELINE_STRATEGY' THEN 1
        ELSE 2
    END,
    strategy_name;



/***************************************************************************************************
SECTION 15.8D — FRONTIER REGISTRY-LINKAGE DIAGNOSTIC
****************************************************************************************************

PURPOSE:
    Summarize whether executive frontier rows are linked to the campaign registry.

BUSINESS PURPOSE:
    Confirm whether the archive-wide frontier output can be referenced through stable campaign IDs.

    This is useful before:
        exporting the frontier summary,
        drafting README results,
        preparing LinkedIn post evidence,
        or selecting rows for a future Validation Summary.

SQL PURPOSE:
    1. Count frontier rows by registry match status.
    2. Identify rows missing module2_run_id.
    3. Identify rows missing validation_evidence_group_id.
    4. Provide a compact registry_linkage_status.

STATUS VALUES:
    FRONTIER_REGISTRY_LINKAGE_READY:
        Every executive frontier row has a matched registry row.

    FRONTIER_REGISTRY_LINKAGE_PARTIAL:
        Some rows have registry mappings and some do not.

    FRONTIER_REGISTRY_LINKAGE_NOT_AVAILABLE:
        No executive frontier rows have registry mappings.

    FRONTIER_REGISTRY_DUPLICATE_REVIEW_REQUIRED:
        At least one frontier row matched duplicate active registry mappings.

BOUNDARY:
    Missing registry linkage does not invalidate strategy frontier metrics.

    It only limits documentation traceability.

***************************************************************************************************/

WITH registry_summary AS (
    SELECT
        COUNT(*) AS executive_frontier_rows,

        COUNT(*) FILTER (
            WHERE frontier_registry_match_status = 'FRONTIER_REGISTRY_MATCHED'
        ) AS registry_matched_rows,

        COUNT(*) FILTER (
            WHERE frontier_registry_match_status = 'FRONTIER_REGISTRY_NOT_FOUND'
        ) AS registry_missing_rows,

        COUNT(*) FILTER (
            WHERE frontier_registry_match_status = 'FRONTIER_REGISTRY_DUPLICATE_MATCH_REVIEW'
        ) AS registry_duplicate_review_rows,

        COUNT(*) FILTER (
            WHERE module2_run_id IS NULL
        ) AS missing_module2_run_id_rows,

        COUNT(*) FILTER (
            WHERE validation_evidence_group_id IS NULL
        ) AS missing_validation_evidence_group_id_rows

    FROM tmp_m2_strategy_frontier_executive_summary
)

SELECT
    executive_frontier_rows,
    registry_matched_rows,
    registry_missing_rows,
    registry_duplicate_review_rows,
    missing_module2_run_id_rows,
    missing_validation_evidence_group_id_rows,

    CASE
        WHEN registry_duplicate_review_rows > 0
            THEN 'FRONTIER_REGISTRY_DUPLICATE_REVIEW_REQUIRED'

        WHEN executive_frontier_rows > 0
         AND registry_matched_rows = executive_frontier_rows
            THEN 'FRONTIER_REGISTRY_LINKAGE_READY'

        WHEN registry_matched_rows > 0
         AND registry_missing_rows > 0
            THEN 'FRONTIER_REGISTRY_LINKAGE_PARTIAL'

        WHEN executive_frontier_rows > 0
         AND registry_matched_rows = 0
            THEN 'FRONTIER_REGISTRY_LINKAGE_NOT_AVAILABLE'

        ELSE 'FRONTIER_REGISTRY_LINKAGE_REVIEW_REQUIRED'
    END AS registry_linkage_status

FROM registry_summary;

0.10 FINAL DECISION TAXONOMY
====================================================================================================

Module 2 uses exactly four final decision_outcome values:

    APPROVE
    COUNTEROFFER
    MANUAL_REVIEW
    DECLINE

APPROVE:
    Clean simulated positive offer outcome as requested.

COUNTEROFFER:
    Simulated positive offer outcome with reduced approved exposure.
    COUNTEROFFER is distinct from APPROVE.

MANUAL_REVIEW:
    Unresolved simulated strategy outcome.
    No approved exposure or approved Expected Loss is assigned.

DECLINE:
    Simulated no-offer outcome using the zero-exposure convention.

CREDIT RISK LEARNING POINT:
    Separating APPROVE from COUNTEROFFER matters.

    A counteroffer is still simulated positive offer exposure, but it is not the same as approving the
    requested structure.

    This distinction allows strategy reviewers to evaluate whether a strategy is preserving access by
    reducing exposure rather than simply approving or declining.

    exposure-treatment fields,
    simulated reason codes,

A preliminary counteroffer route does not guarantee a final feasible counteroffer.

Final COUNTEROFFER is assigned only after approved exposure, approved PTI, and approved Expected Loss
feasibility have been evaluated.

====================================================================================================
0.18 SQL PATTERNS USED THROUGHOUT MODULE 2
====================================================================================================

This module repeatedly uses a small number of SQL patterns.

Understanding these patterns will make the rest of the file easier to read.

1. CREATE TEMP TABLE ... AS SELECT
    Used to materialize a staging layer.

    Why:
        It makes intermediate transformation logic inspectable.

2. WITH common_table_expressions AS (...)
    Used to break complex logic into named steps.

    Why:
        It allows readers to follow the transformation path instead of reading one giant nested query.

3. SELECT DISTINCT
    Used when converting applicant-grain output into run-grain helper tables.

    Why:
        Applicant-level rows repeat run metadata. DISTINCT collapses that repeated metadata into a
        single run key.

4. COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE condition)
    Used for compact validation and outcome-rate logic.

    Why:
        It lets one query calculate many conditional counts without separate subqueries.

5. NULLIF(denominator, 0)
    Used to prevent divide-by-zero errors.

    Why:
        Validation and segmentation queries should remain stable even when a population segment has
        zero rows.

6. COALESCE(value, fallback)
    Used when preserving portfolio-impact metrics or fallback metadata.

    Why:
        It makes NULL handling explicit.

7. IS DISTINCT FROM
    Used for safe equality checks when NULLs may exist.

    Why:
        Unlike ordinary equality, IS DISTINCT FROM treats NULL versus non-NULL as a comparable
        difference.

8. ROW_NUMBER() OVER (...)
    Used for deterministic ranking.

    Why:
        It supports top reason-code selection, top segment selection, and duplicate-safe registry
        mapping.

====================================================================================================
0.19 HOW TO INTERPRET RATES AND SHARES
====================================================================================================

This module uses several kinds of rates.

Users should preserve denominator discipline.

approval_rate:
    APPROVE rows / all applications in the relevant population.

counteroffer_rate:
    COUNTEROFFER rows / all applications in the relevant population.

manual_review_rate:
    MANUAL_REVIEW rows / all applications in the relevant population.

decline_rate:
    DECLINE rows / all applications in the relevant population.

simulated_offer_exposure_rate:
    APPROVE + COUNTEROFFER rows / all applications in the relevant population.

approval_share_of_offers:
    APPROVE rows / simulated positive offer-exposure rows.

counteroffer_share_of_offers:
    COUNTEROFFER rows / simulated positive offer-exposure rows.

approved_expected_loss_rate:
    total approved Expected Loss / total approved amount.

CREDIT RISK LEARNING POINT:
    A strategy can have a high approval rate but still be weak if approved Expected Loss is too high.

    A strategy can have lower approval but stronger risk discipline if approved Expected Loss falls
    meaningfully and risk ordering improves.

    A strategy can preserve access through counteroffers while reducing approved exposure.

    That is why Module 2 evaluates multiple metrics rather than a single approval-rate statistic.

        and all downstream strategy logic.

    Do not assume old temporary parameter tables from a prior session are still valid.

HOW TO MODIFY THIS SECTION FOR A NEW RUN:
    For a new Module 2 strategy run, edit the active strategy row in Section 2.2 first.

    The most common fields to update are:
        strategy_name,
        strategy_run_id,
        module1_input_source,
        source_module1_scenario_set_name,
        source_module1_scenario_name,
        source_population_id,
        synthetic estimated-risk thresholds,
        PTI thresholds,
        DTI thresholds,
        archive_run_flag,
        strategy_archive_reset_mode,
        campaign_registry_required_flag.

    For product-level strategy changes, edit Section 2.4 product policy defaults.

    For run-roadmap / documentation changes, edit Section 2.6 campaign registry rows.

    For Section 13 matched comparison changes, edit Section 2.8 comparison registry rows and the
    active_comparison_flag.

PARAMETER GOVERNANCE PRINCIPLE:
    Downstream CASE logic should consume strategy and product parameters rather than silently
    embedding ungoverned thresholds.

    Users should tune Module 2 first through:
        tmp_module2_strategy_params
        tmp_module2_product_policy_params

    before rewriting downstream decision, routing, exposure, or reason-code logic.

    This is a core governance principle:
        strategy behavior should be visible in a parameter card before it appears in decision logic.

CREDIT RISK CONCEPTS TAUGHT BY THIS SECTION:
    Synthetic estimated-risk thresholds:
        Represent strategy tolerance for the Module 1 estimated_pd field, interpreted as a synthetic
        estimated-PD proxy.

    PTI thresholds:
        Represent payment burden tolerance. PTI is a borrower affordability concept:
            payment obligation / monthly income.

    DTI thresholds:
        Represent existing obligation capacity. In Module 2 V1.0, DTI is not directly corrected by
        reducing requested exposure.

    Requested Expected Loss thresholds:
        Control risk sensitivity using requested-exposure Expected Loss from Module 1.

    Approved Expected Loss caps:
        Control post-treatment approved-exposure economics after Module 2 exposure reduction.

    Counteroffer controls:
        Determine when reduced-exposure treatment is allowed and how conservative that treatment
        must be.

    Archive controls:
        Determine whether the latest-run output becomes governed historical evidence.

    Campaign registry IDs:
        Determine how technical SQL outputs connect to executive and validation documentation.

CAMPAIGN REGISTRY GOVERNANCE PRINCIPLE:
    Module 1 scenario lineage and Module 2 strategy metadata remain the technical source of truth.

    Campaign IDs such as:
        module1_run_id
        module2_run_id
        showcase_id
        comparison_group_id
        validation_evidence_group_id

    are documentation and evidence-linkage metadata.

    They do not replace:
        module1_scenario_set_name
        module1_scenario_name
        population_id
        strategy_set_name
        strategy_name
        strategy_version
        application_id

    They help connect:
        run roadmap
        → SQL output
        → archive slice
        → comparison result
        → executive evidence row
        → validation evidence row
        → parameter snapshot
        → future Validation Summary claim.

SQL DESIGN PRINCIPLE:
    Section 2 uses a mix of temporary and persistent objects.

    Temporary objects:
        tmp_module2_strategy_params
        tmp_module2_product_policy_params

        These exist for the current execution session and drive the current run.

    Persistent registry objects:
        credit_decisioning_sim.strategy_run_campaign_registry
        credit_decisioning_sim.strategy_comparison_campaign_registry

        These persist across runs and provide the governed run roadmap.

    This separation matters:
        parameters drive the current execution;
        registries organize the campaign evidence across executions.

DEFAULT THRESHOLD INTERPRETATION:
    Defaults in this section are initial synthetic strategy defaults.

    They are:
        intended for strategy simulation,
        expected to be reviewed through QA and strategy tuning,
        not production underwriting policy,
        not empirical calibration,
        not a calibrated default model,
        not regulatory policy,
        not real customer treatment logic.

OPERATING GUIDANCE:
    For a formal campaign run:
        1. Confirm the Module 1 source scenario fields.
        2. Confirm the Module 2 strategy identity.
        3. Confirm the current strategy exists in credit_decisioning_sim.strategy_run_campaign_registry.
        4. Confirm any intended Section 13 comparison exists in
           credit_decisioning_sim.strategy_comparison_campaign_registry.
        5. Keep campaign_registry_required_flag = TRUE.
        6. Run Section 3 gatekeepers before building downstream strategy logic.

    For ad hoc development:
        campaign_registry_required_flag may be set to FALSE, but formal validation evidence should
        use registry-matched runs.

INTERPRETATION BOUNDARY:
    Section 2 defines the active strategy posture and campaign roadmap.

    It does not prove the strategy behaved as expected.

    Evidence of actual behavior comes later from:
        Section 11 latest-run output,
        Section 12 archive persistence,
        Section 13 matched comparison,
        Section 14 QA,
        Section 15 strategy frontier,
        Section 16 evidence capture.

BOUNDARY:
    Section 2 defines governed controls and campaign metadata.
    Section 2 does not consume Module 1 rows.
    Section 2 does not create decision outcomes.
    Section 2 does not assign reason codes.
    Section 2 does not calculate approved exposure.
    Section 2 does not calculate approved Expected Loss.
    Section 2 does not insert archive rows.
    Section 2 does not perform matched comparison.
    Section 2 does not perform QA validation.
    Section 2 does not draft written validation conclusions.

COMMON MISUSE TO AVOID:
    Do not treat strategy_run_id as the archive replacement key.
    Do not treat campaign IDs as replacements for technical SQL lineage.
    Do not interpret synthetic estimated-risk thresholds as calibrated production PD cutoffs.
    Do not interpret product-policy values as approved production underwriting limits.
    Do not rewrite downstream CASE logic when a parameter change would answer the business question.
    Do not use formal validation evidence without registry-matched campaign IDs.

***************************************************************************************************/



/***************************************************************************************************
SECTION 2.1 — STRATEGY PARAMETER TABLE
****************************************************************************************************

BUSINESS PURPOSE:
    Define the single active Module 2 strategy configuration for the current run.

    This table is the active strategy card.

    It identifies:
        the Module 2 strategy,
        the Module 1 source slice,
        the archive behavior,
        the synthetic-risk appetite,
        the affordability appetite,
        the DTI capacity posture,
        diagnostic buffers,
        policy-stop trigger controls,
        reason-code conventions,
        exposure conventions,
        and the registry requirement for formal evidence capture.

SQL PURPOSE:
    Create a temporary parameter table containing strategy identity, source selection, archive
    controls, thresholds, rule controls, decision conventions, and registry requirements.

WHY THIS TABLE EXISTS:
    Module 2 should be strategy-parameterized rather than hard-coded.

    The same downstream SQL pipeline can simulate different strategies by changing this parameter row
    and the product-policy parameter rows.

CARDINALITY REQUIREMENT:
    Exactly one row should have:
        active_strategy_flag = TRUE

    Section 3 enforces this.

SQL MECHANICS:
    CREATE TEMP TABLE creates a session-scoped table.

    ON COMMIT PRESERVE ROWS keeps the temporary parameter row available across transaction
    boundaries during the same session.

    This is important because the downstream staged SQL blocks read this table repeatedly.

    Section 1 drops this table at the beginning of a clean full run so stale strategy parameters
    cannot leak into the next execution.

CREDIT RISK TEACHING POINT:
    Credit strategy configuration is not just a list of cutoffs.

    A strategy card combines multiple governance dimensions:
        risk appetite,
        affordability appetite,
        DTI capacity,
        product controls,
        archive controls,
        evidence traceability,
        and final output conventions.

****************************************************************************************************/

CREATE TEMP TABLE tmp_module2_strategy_params (
    /***********************************************************************************************
    Active strategy cardinality.

    active_strategy_flag identifies the one strategy row used by the current run.

    Section 3 fails if:
        zero rows are active,
        or more than one row is active.

    This prevents ambiguous strategy execution.
    ***********************************************************************************************/
    active_strategy_flag                         BOOLEAN,


    /***********************************************************************************************
    Strategy identity.

    These fields identify the downstream Module 2 strategy.

    They should not be confused with Module 1 scenario fields.

    module2_model_version:
        version of the Module 2 engine.

    strategy_set_name:
        strategy family / campaign grouping.

    strategy_name:
        specific strategy posture, such as BASELINE_STRATEGY or TIGHTER_SYNTHETIC_RISK_STRATEGY.

    strategy_version:
        version of the strategy definition.

    strategy_run_id and strategy_run_ts:
        audit metadata for traceability.

        These are not archive replacement keys and not matched-comparison keys.
    ***********************************************************************************************/
    module2_model_version                        TEXT,
    strategy_set_name                            TEXT,
    strategy_name                                TEXT,
    strategy_version                             TEXT,
    strategy_run_id                              TEXT,
    strategy_run_ts                              TIMESTAMP,


    /***********************************************************************************************
    Formal campaign registry control.

    campaign_registry_required_flag:
        TRUE means the current technical run key should match exactly one active row in
        credit_decisioning_sim.strategy_run_campaign_registry.

        FALSE allows ad hoc development runs to proceed with fallback evidence metadata.

    This flag does not affect decision logic.
    It only governs evidence traceability expectations.

    Interpretation:
        TRUE is appropriate for formal campaign runs.
        FALSE may be useful during exploratory development, but should not be used for final
        validation-summary evidence unless intentionally documented.
    ***********************************************************************************************/
    campaign_registry_required_flag              BOOLEAN,


    /***********************************************************************************************
    Module 1 source selection.

    module1_input_source:
        LATEST or ARCHIVE.

    source_module1_scenario_set_name:
        required when ARCHIVE is selected.

    source_module1_scenario_name:
        required when ARCHIVE is selected.

    source_population_id:
        required when ARCHIVE is selected.

    Credit risk interpretation:
        These fields decide which upstream synthetic population and risk environment Module 2 will
        consume.

    SQL interpretation:
        Section 4 reads these values to decide which Module 1 table and scenario slice to select.
    ***********************************************************************************************/
    module1_input_source                         TEXT,
    source_module1_scenario_set_name             TEXT,
    source_module1_scenario_name                 TEXT,
    source_population_id                         TEXT,


    /***********************************************************************************************
    Archive controls.

    archive_run_flag:
        TRUE means Section 12 may persist the latest-run output to archive.

        FALSE means Section 12 should skip archive insertion.

    strategy_archive_reset_mode:
        governs what existing archive rows are deleted before inserting the current run, if any.

    These controls do not affect decision outcomes.
    They govern historical persistence.
    ***********************************************************************************************/
    archive_run_flag                             BOOLEAN,
    strategy_archive_reset_mode                  TEXT,


    /***********************************************************************************************
    Global synthetic estimated-risk thresholds.

    estimated_pd is the finalized Module 1 SQL field name.

    These thresholds interpret estimated_pd as the synthetic estimated-PD proxy.

    Credit risk interpretation:
        Lower estimated_pd indicates lower synthetic estimated risk.
        Higher estimated_pd indicates higher synthetic estimated risk.

    Strategy interpretation:
        These thresholds define the global synthetic-risk tolerance posture before product-specific
        exposure treatment is applied downstream.
    ***********************************************************************************************/
    approve_max_estimated_pd_proxy               NUMERIC(12,6),
    counteroffer_max_estimated_pd_proxy          NUMERIC(12,6),
    review_max_estimated_pd_proxy                NUMERIC(12,6),
    decline_min_estimated_pd_proxy               NUMERIC(12,6),


    /***********************************************************************************************
    Global PTI thresholds.

    PTI means payment-to-income ratio.

    Product-specific PTI thresholds drive product PTI segmentation and rules.

    These global values provide high-level consistency controls and fallback context.

    Credit risk interpretation:
        PTI is the affordability bridge from product structure to repayment stress.
    ***********************************************************************************************/
    global_approve_max_pti                       NUMERIC(12,6),
    global_review_max_pti                        NUMERIC(12,6),
    global_decline_min_pti                       NUMERIC(12,6),


    /***********************************************************************************************
    DTI thresholds.

    DTI is debt-to-income ratio.

    DTI reflects existing obligation capacity rather than the requested loan payment alone.

    In Module 2 V1.0, DTI is not directly corrected through counteroffer exposure reduction.

    This means a high-DTI row may still route to review or decline even if requested exposure could
    be reduced.
    ***********************************************************************************************/
    approve_max_dti                              NUMERIC(12,6),
    review_max_dti                               NUMERIC(12,6),
    decline_min_dti                              NUMERIC(12,6),


    /***********************************************************************************************
    Diagnostic segmentation controls.

    borderline_threshold_buffer_pct:
        Governs how close a value must be to a strategy threshold to be tagged as borderline.

        Example:
            0.050000 means "within 5% of the threshold value."

        This is not a production policy tolerance.
        This is a diagnostic segmentation buffer used only to identify threshold-adjacent synthetic
        profiles before decision rules are applied.

    SQL interpretation:
        Section 5 uses this parameter when creating borderline_profile_flag.
    ***********************************************************************************************/
    borderline_threshold_buffer_pct              NUMERIC(12,6),


    /***********************************************************************************************
    Rule-control parameters for Section 6 trigger construction.

    These parameters control simulated trigger flags only.

    They do not assign final decision_outcome.
    They do not create reason codes.
    They do not represent production underwriting policy.

    Section 6 uses them to answer:
        "Which simulated policy conditions are triggered?"

    Later sections answer:
        "Which preliminary route is selected?"
        "Is reduced-exposure treatment feasible?"
        "Which final simulated outcome is assigned?"
        "Which simulated reason codes explain that outcome?"
    ***********************************************************************************************/
    bankruptcy_policy_stop_enabled               BOOLEAN,
    major_derogatory_policy_stop_enabled         BOOLEAN,
    severe_delinquency_policy_stop_enabled       BOOLEAN,
    severe_delinquency_count_threshold           INTEGER,
    high_utilization_review_enabled              BOOLEAN,
    high_utilization_review_threshold            NUMERIC(12,6),
    low_score_review_enabled                     BOOLEAN,
    low_score_review_threshold                   INTEGER,


    /***********************************************************************************************
    Decision convention controls.

    approve_reason_code:
        default simulated primary reason code for clean approvals.

    reason_code_required_flag:
        tells downstream QA that every final row should receive reason-code evidence.

    simulated_offer_exposure_flag_enabled:
        enables the positive-offer exposure convention for APPROVE and COUNTEROFFER rows.

    manual_review_approved_amount_convention:
        expected convention for unresolved manual-review approved exposure.

    decline_approved_amount_convention:
        expected convention for no-offer declined exposure.

    approved_el_decline_convention:
        expected convention for approved Expected Loss on declined rows.

    approved_el_manual_review_convention:
        expected convention for approved Expected Loss on unresolved manual-review rows.

    allow_approved_amount_above_requested_flag:
        protects against approved exposure exceeding requested exposure.
    ***********************************************************************************************/
    approve_reason_code                          TEXT,
    reason_code_required_flag                    BOOLEAN,
    simulated_offer_exposure_flag_enabled        BOOLEAN,
    manual_review_approved_amount_convention     TEXT,
    decline_approved_amount_convention           TEXT,
    approved_el_decline_convention               TEXT,
    approved_el_manual_review_convention         TEXT,
    allow_approved_amount_above_requested_flag   BOOLEAN,


    /***********************************************************************************************
    Final decision-resolution control.

    failed_counteroffer_resolution:
        Governs how preliminary COUNTEROFFER routes resolve when Section 8 determines that no viable
        reduced-exposure treatment exists.

    Allowed values:
        MANUAL_REVIEW
        DECLINE

    Default:
        MANUAL_REVIEW

    Interpretation:
        A failed counteroffer is routed to MANUAL_REVIEW by default because higher-priority hard
        simulated policy stops, severe synthetic estimated-risk, and severe DTI have already routed
        to DECLINE before counteroffer feasibility is evaluated.

    Boundary:
        This is a simulated strategy-control parameter, not production underwriting policy.
    ***********************************************************************************************/
    failed_counteroffer_resolution               TEXT
) ON COMMIT PRESERVE ROWS;
