    Section 13 is a selected matched comparison framework.

    It compares one baseline and one challenger strategy slice by application_id.

    Section 15 is a frontier control-tower view.

    It summarizes all archived strategy / scenario slices and turns them into:
        frontier metrics,
        baseline-relative deltas,
        efficiency indicators,
        posture classifications,
        segment highlights,
        registry-aware executive story fields,
        and executive-ready result tables.

WHY SECTION 15 IS DIFFERENT FROM SECTION 14:
    Section 14 validates the latest-run output.

    Section 15 summarizes archived strategy tradeoffs.

    Section 15 assumes upstream latest-run and archive validation have already occurred.

    Section 15 does not replace Section 14 QA.

WHY SECTION 15 IS REGISTRY-AWARE:
    Formal campaign runs use stable run IDs such as:
        module1_run_id
        module2_run_id
        showcase_id
        comparison_group_id
        validation_evidence_group_id

    Those IDs are easier to reference in:
        README summaries,
        LinkedIn posts,
        validation-summary sections,
        comparison narratives,
        and executive review.

    Section 15 therefore enriches the executive frontier output with campaign registry fields where
    a registry row exists for the archived technical strategy / scenario key.

REGISTRY BOUNDARY:
    Registry IDs are documentation and evidence-linkage metadata.

    They do not replace the technical SQL key:
        strategy_set_name
        strategy_name
        strategy_version
        module1_scenario_set_name
        module1_scenario_name
        population_id

    Section 15 does not require a registry match.

    Missing registry mapping is surfaced through:
        frontier_registry_match_status = 'FRONTIER_REGISTRY_NOT_FOUND'

    This is a review / documentation signal, not a strategy-output failure.

STRATEGY FRONTIER CONCEPT:
    A strategy frontier is not a single "best strategy" ranking.

    It is a structured view of tradeoffs among:
        access / simulated offer exposure,
        approved exposure,
        approved Expected Loss,
        approved Expected Loss rate,
        offered-population synthetic estimated-risk profile,
        approved PTI quality,
        counteroffer reliance,
        manual-review burden,
        decline concentration,
        and reason-code movement.

    A growth-oriented point may increase simulated offer exposure and approved amount while increasing
    approved Expected Loss.

    A risk-discipline point may reduce approved Expected Loss while lowering simulated offer exposure.

    A counteroffer-management point may preserve access through reduced-exposure treatment.

    A manual-review-reduction point may reduce unresolved outcomes while increasing final no-offer
    outcomes.

    These are simulated strategy tradeoffs, not production recommendations.

PURE STRATEGY FRONTIER VS SCENARIO × STRATEGY FRONTIER:
    Pure Module 2 strategy frontier:
        Compare multiple Module 2 strategies within the same Module 1 scenario and population.

        This is strongest for isolating downstream Module 2 strategy effects.

    Scenario × strategy frontier:
        Compare archived outcomes across multiple Module 1 scenarios and Module 2 strategies.

        This is useful as an executive control-tower view, but users must preserve the distinction
        between upstream Module 1 scenario effects and downstream Module 2 strategy effects.

BASELINE-RELATIVE DELTA BOUNDARY:
    Baseline-relative deltas are calculated only where a BASELINE_STRATEGY exists under the same:
        strategy_set_name
        module1_scenario_set_name
        module1_scenario_name
        population_id

    If no baseline is available, baseline-relative fields are NULL and baseline_available_flag is
    FALSE.

    Missing baseline is not a failure.

    It means the archived frontier point can be summarized but cannot be interpreted as a baseline-
    relative strategy delta.

ESTIMATED_PD BOUNDARY:
    estimated_pd remains the finalized Module 1 SQL field name.

    In Section 15, estimated_pd is interpreted as the synthetic estimated-PD proxy.

    Section 15 does not recalculate estimated_pd.
    Section 15 does not calibrate estimated_pd.
    Section 15 does not validate production default forecasting.

REQUESTED VS APPROVED EXPECTED LOSS:
    requested_expected_loss_amount:
        Requested-exposure Expected Loss carried from Module 1.

    approved_expected_loss_amount:
        Module 2 approved-exposure Expected Loss after final simulated exposure treatment.

    approved_expected_loss_rate:
        total_approved_expected_loss_amount / total_approved_amount.

        This is a synthetic strategy frontier metric.

        It is not a production loss-rate forecast.

SIMULATED OFFER EXPOSURE BOUNDARY:
    simulated_offer_exposure_flag identifies simulated positive offer exposure.

    It is TRUE for:
        APPROVE
        COUNTEROFFER

    It is FALSE for:
        MANUAL_REVIEW
        DECLINE

    It does not imply:
        operational account creation,
        booked exposure,
        funded exposure,
        production approval,
        customer treatment,
        or real applicant treatment.

SIMULATED REASON-CODE BOUNDARY:
    primary_reason_code and primary_reason_family remain simulated strategy explanation fields.

    They support:
        frontier interpretation,
        QA review,
        executive storytelling,
        README summaries,
        LinkedIn summaries,
        validation evidence,
        and strategy comparison.

    They are not:
        customer communications,
        regulatory notices,
        adverse-action reasons,
        production compliance determinations,
        or fair-lending conclusions.

EFFICIENCY METRIC BOUNDARY:
    Section 15 efficiency metrics are comparative synthetic strategy metrics.

    They are not:
        profitability metrics,
        revenue metrics,
        pricing metrics,
        margin metrics,
        capital metrics,
        funding-cost metrics,
        or risk-adjusted return metrics.

    Those belong to a future Module 3 economics layer.

SQL CONCEPTS TAUGHT IN THIS SECTION:
    CREATE TEMP TABLE ... AS:
        Materializes temporary frontier helper tables for current-session review and evidence capture.

    CTEs:
        Break complex frontier calculations into interpretable stages such as slice summary,
        reason-code shares, baseline deltas, efficiency metrics, and classifications.

    COUNT(*) FILTER:
        Calculates outcome-specific counts and rates without removing the rest of the archived slice.

    COALESCE:
        Converts unresolved or no-offer approved exposure / approved Expected Loss to zero when
        calculating all-application portfolio-impact metrics.

    NULLIF:
        Prevents divide-by-zero when calculating rates, ratios, and efficiency metrics.

    Window functions:
        ROW_NUMBER identifies top reason-code records and registry matches.
        RANK creates executive frontier ranks within each scenario / strategy-set group.
        COUNT(*) OVER creates group-level counts without collapsing rows.

    LEFT JOIN:
        Preserves frontier rows when optional baseline, reason-code, or registry metadata is absent.

    UNION ALL:
        Builds product, score-band, and product × score segment views in one segment-highlight table.

    CASE:
        Converts metric patterns into readable frontier status labels and executive quadrant labels.

READ-ONLY BOUNDARY:
    Section 15 does not insert archive rows.
    Section 15 does not delete archive rows.
    Section 15 does not update archive rows.
    Section 15 does not modify credit_decisioning_sim.strategy_decisions.
    Section 15 does not modify credit_decisioning_sim.strategy_decisions_archive.
    Section 15 does not modify campaign registry rows.
    Section 15 does not modify strategy parameters.
    Section 15 does not modify product policy parameters.
    Section 15 does not recalculate decision_outcome.
    Section 15 does not recalculate approved exposure.
    Section 15 does not recalculate approved Expected Loss.
    Section 15 does not reassign simulated reason codes.
    Section 15 does not draft the BRD or Validation Summary.

GOVERNANCE ROLE:
    Section 15 converts archived strategy outputs into a compact, executive-readable evidence layer.

    It supports:
        strategy frontier review,
        campaign-run interpretation,
        README result summaries,
        LinkedIn post storytelling,
        Validation Summary evidence selection,
        and future Module 3 economics design.

COMMON MISUSE TO AVOID:
    Do not treat frontier_position_type as a production recommendation.
    Do not treat executive_frontier_quadrant as a final strategy ranking.
    Do not compare different Module 1 scenarios and call the result a pure Module 2 strategy effect.
    Do not interpret approved_expected_loss_rate as a production loss forecast.
    Do not interpret simulated offer exposure as booked or funded exposure.
    Do not interpret reason-code movement as customer communication language.
    Do not treat missing registry mapping as a strategy-output failure.
    Do not use Section 15 as a substitute for Section 14 validation.

***************************************************************************************************/



/***************************************************************************************************
SECTION 15.0 — FRONTIER SCOPE AND ARCHIVE READINESS SNAPSHOT
****************************************************************************************************

PURPOSE:
    Confirm that the governed archive exists and provide a quick archive-level readiness snapshot
    before creating strategy frontier outputs.

BUSINESS PURPOSE:
    Confirm whether the archive contains enough completed strategy / scenario slices to support
    meaningful frontier analysis.

SQL PURPOSE:
    1. Confirm credit_decisioning_sim.strategy_decisions_archive exists.
    2. Count archived rows.
    3. Count distinct archived application_id values.
    4. Count archived strategy × scenario slices.
    5. Count Module 1 scenario / population slices.
    6. Count Module 2 strategy versions.
    7. Display archive timestamp range.
    8. Assign a frontier_scope_status.

FRONTIER READINESS INTERPRETATION:
    FRONTIER_NOT_READY_ARCHIVE_EMPTY:
        No archived rows exist.

    FRONTIER_INVENTORY_ONLY_SINGLE_ARCHIVED_SLICE:
        Only one archived strategy / scenario slice exists.
        Section 15 can summarize inventory, but it cannot yet show strategy tradeoffs.

    FRONTIER_READY_FOR_MULTI_STRATEGY_REVIEW:
        At least two Module 2 strategy versions exist in the archive.
        Section 15 can begin to show multi-strategy frontier tradeoffs.

    FRONTIER_AVAILABLE_FOR_ARCHIVE_REVIEW:
        Archive contains rows and can be summarized, though richer frontier interpretation may depend
        on the mix of scenarios and strategies available.

WHAT TO LOOK FOR:
    archived_rows:
        Should be positive for meaningful Section 15 output.

    archived_strategy_scenario_slice_count:
        One means inventory only.
        More than one means the archive can support frontier review.

    module2_strategy_version_count:
        Two or more is the strongest signal that Module 2 strategy tradeoffs can be reviewed.

REVIEW TRIGGERS:
    Archive table missing:
        Section 12 has not created / persisted the archive.

    Archive empty:
        Section 15 cannot produce frontier tradeoffs.

    Single archived slice:
        Section 15 can show inventory, but baseline-relative and multi-strategy interpretation will
        be limited.

SQL MECHANICS:
    TO_REGCLASS:
        Checks whether the archive table exists before the query references it.

    COUNT(DISTINCT concatenated key):
        Counts distinct multi-column frontier slices using a readable string key.

        PostgreSQL also supports COUNT(DISTINCT (col1, col2, ...)), but the concatenated form keeps
        the current accepted logic intact.

    CASE:
        Converts archive counts into a readable frontier scope status.

BOUNDARY:
    This is a read-only diagnostic.

    It does not require a baseline strategy to exist.
    It does not require campaign registry mapping.
    It does not modify archive rows.
    It does not validate the latest-run output.
    It does not perform matched comparison.

***************************************************************************************************/

DO $$
BEGIN
    /*-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    Dependency check:
        Section 15 is archive-backed.

    Failure interpretation:
        If this table does not exist, Section 12 has not created / reused the governed archive yet.
    -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
    IF TO_REGCLASS('credit_decisioning_sim.strategy_decisions_archive') IS NULL THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION
            'Module 2 Section 15 failure: credit_decisioning_sim.strategy_decisions_archive does not exist. Run Section 12 before Section 15.';
    END IF;
END $$;


SELECT
    /***********************************************************************************************
    Static label so the output grid is self-describing when copied into QA notes or executive review.
    ***********************************************************************************************/
    'SECTION_15_FRONTIER_SCOPE' AS diagnostic_name,

    /***********************************************************************************************
    Basic archive size.

    archived_rows:
        total number of archived applicant-level strategy rows.

    distinct_archived_application_ids:
        distinct application_id values across the whole archive. This is not expected to equal
        archived_rows when multiple strategy / scenario slices exist because the same application_id
        can appear in multiple archived slices.
    ***********************************************************************************************/
    COUNT(*) AS archived_rows,
    COUNT(DISTINCT application_id) AS distinct_archived_application_ids,

    /***********************************************************************************************
    Count archived strategy / scenario / population slices.

    Interpretation:
        This is the number of completed frontier points available before collapsing into Section 15
        summary tables.
    ***********************************************************************************************/
    COUNT(DISTINCT
        strategy_set_name
        || '|' || strategy_name
        || '|' || strategy_version
        || '|' || module1_scenario_set_name
        || '|' || module1_scenario_name
        || '|' || population_id
    ) AS archived_strategy_scenario_slice_count,

    /***********************************************************************************************
    Count upstream Module 1 scenario / population slices.

    Interpretation:
        More than one means the archive contains multiple upstream population / scenario conditions.
        Cross-scenario review is useful, but pure Module 2 strategy comparison should hold these
        fields constant.
    ***********************************************************************************************/
    COUNT(DISTINCT
        module1_scenario_set_name
        || '|' || module1_scenario_name
        || '|' || population_id
    ) AS module1_scenario_population_slice_count,

    /***********************************************************************************************
    Count distinct Module 2 strategy identities.

    Interpretation:
        Two or more strategy identities are needed for multi-strategy frontier review.
    ***********************************************************************************************/
    COUNT(DISTINCT
        strategy_set_name
        || '|' || strategy_name
        || '|' || strategy_version
    ) AS module2_strategy_version_count,

    /***********************************************************************************************
    Archive persistence timestamp range.

    These are audit timestamps only. They do not define comparison grain or frontier rank.
    ***********************************************************************************************/
    MIN(archive_inserted_ts) AS min_archive_inserted_ts,
    MAX(archive_inserted_ts) AS max_archive_inserted_ts,

    /***********************************************************************************************
    Frontier readiness label.

    This status tells reviewers whether Section 15 can be interpreted as:
        no archive,
        inventory only,
        multi-strategy frontier,
        or broader archive review.
    ***********************************************************************************************/
    CASE
        WHEN COUNT(*) = 0
            THEN 'FRONTIER_NOT_READY_ARCHIVE_EMPTY'

        WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT
                strategy_set_name
                || '|' || strategy_name
                || '|' || strategy_version
                || '|' || module1_scenario_set_name
                || '|' || module1_scenario_name
                || '|' || population_id
             ) = 1
            THEN 'FRONTIER_INVENTORY_ONLY_SINGLE_ARCHIVED_SLICE'

        WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT
                strategy_set_name
                || '|' || strategy_name
                || '|' || strategy_version
             ) >= 2
            THEN 'FRONTIER_READY_FOR_MULTI_STRATEGY_REVIEW'

        ELSE 'FRONTIER_AVAILABLE_FOR_ARCHIVE_REVIEW'
    END AS frontier_scope_status

FROM credit_decisioning_sim.strategy_decisions_archive;



/***************************************************************************************************
SECTION 15.0A — OPTIONAL CAMPAIGN REGISTRY MAP FOR FRONTIER OUTPUTS
****************************************************************************************************

PURPOSE:
    Create a temporary registry map that enriches archived frontier points with formal campaign run
    IDs when available.

BUSINESS PURPOSE:
    Make Section 15 usable as a standalone export layer for README, LinkedIn, executive review, and
    validation-summary planning.

    Section 16 already captures registry-backed evidence for the current run.

    Section 15.0A extends similar readability to the archive-wide frontier output.

SQL PURPOSE:
    1. Create tmp_m2_strategy_frontier_campaign_registry_map.
    2. If credit_decisioning_sim.strategy_run_campaign_registry exists, load active registry mappings.
    3. If the registry table does not exist, create an empty map with the expected schema.
    4. Avoid failing Section 15 solely because registry metadata is unavailable.
    5. Prevent duplicate active registry rows from multiplying frontier rows by ranking to one row
       per technical key and surfacing registry_match_count.

REGISTRY MAP GRAIN:
    One row per technical run key when an active registry row exists:

        module1_scenario_set_name
        module1_scenario_name
        population_id
        strategy_set_name
        strategy_name
        strategy_version

REGISTRY STATUS VALUES:
    FRONTIER_REGISTRY_MATCHED:
        Exactly one active registry row matched the technical frontier key.

    FRONTIER_REGISTRY_DUPLICATE_MATCH_REVIEW:
        More than one active registry row matched the same technical frontier key.
        Section 15 selects the first ranked row to avoid duplicate frontier output rows, but the
        duplicate status should be reviewed.

    FRONTIER_REGISTRY_NOT_FOUND:
        No active registry row matched the technical frontier key.
        This is not a Section 15 failure.

WHAT TO LOOK FOR:
    Registry matched rows are preferred for formal documentation.

    Missing registry rows do not invalidate frontier metrics, but they limit evidence traceability.

    Duplicate registry rows should be reviewed because they can create conflicting campaign IDs for
    the same technical run key.

SQL MECHANICS:
    TO_REGCLASS:
        Checks whether the persistent campaign registry exists.

    DO $$:
        Allows conditional object creation.

    ROW_NUMBER:
        Selects one registry row when duplicate active registry rows exist for the same technical key.

    COUNT(*) OVER:
        Records how many active registry rows matched the same key so duplicate-mapping risk remains
        visible.

BOUNDARY:
    This section reads registry metadata only.

    It does not insert, update, or delete registry rows.
    It does not change strategy results.
    It does not change archive rows.

***************************************************************************************************/

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS tmp_m2_strategy_frontier_campaign_registry_map;

DO $$
BEGIN
    IF TO_REGCLASS('credit_decisioning_sim.strategy_run_campaign_registry') IS NULL THEN

        /*******************************************************************************************
        Registry table is unavailable.

        SQL mechanics:
            Create an empty registry map with the expected output schema.

        Why this matters:
            Later Section 15 queries can LEFT JOIN to this map without failing.

        Interpretation:
            Empty registry map means frontier metrics can still be reviewed, but formal campaign IDs
            are not available from Section 15.
        *******************************************************************************************/
        CREATE TEMP TABLE tmp_m2_strategy_frontier_campaign_registry_map (
            module1_run_id                       TEXT,
            module2_run_id                       TEXT,
            run_sequence_number                  INTEGER,

            showcase_id                          TEXT,
            showcase_name                        TEXT,
            comparison_group_id                  TEXT,
            validation_evidence_group_id         TEXT,

            module1_scenario_set_name            TEXT,
            module1_scenario_name                TEXT,
            population_id                        TEXT,

            strategy_set_name                    TEXT,
            strategy_name                        TEXT,
            strategy_version                     TEXT,

            readme_storyline_label               TEXT,
            linkedin_post_sequence               INTEGER,
            validation_summary_section_hint       TEXT,

            registry_active_flag                 BOOLEAN,
            registry_match_count                 BIGINT,
            frontier_registry_match_status        TEXT
        ) ON COMMIT PRESERVE ROWS;

    ELSE

        /*******************************************************************************************
        Registry table is available.

        Build a one-row-per-technical-key active registry map.

        SQL mechanics:
            registry_ranked first calculates:
                registry_match_count — how many active registry rows share the same technical key.
                registry_rank        — deterministic row number used to select one mapping.

            The final SELECT keeps registry_rank = 1 so frontier rows are not multiplied.

        Governance interpretation:
            If registry_match_count > 1, Section 15 keeps the frontier output stable but flags the
            mapping as FRONTIER_REGISTRY_DUPLICATE_MATCH_REVIEW.
        *******************************************************************************************/
        CREATE TEMP TABLE tmp_m2_strategy_frontier_campaign_registry_map
        ON COMMIT PRESERVE ROWS
        AS
        WITH registry_ranked AS (
            SELECT
                /***********************************************************************************
                Campaign identifiers used for documentation and evidence traceability.
                ***********************************************************************************/
                r.module1_run_id,
                r.module2_run_id,
                r.run_sequence_number,

                r.showcase_id,
                r.showcase_name,
                r.comparison_group_id,
                r.validation_evidence_group_id,

                /***********************************************************************************
                Technical Module 1 + Module 2 frontier key.
                ***********************************************************************************/
                r.module1_scenario_set_name,
                r.module1_scenario_name,
                r.population_id,

                r.strategy_set_name,
                r.strategy_name,
                r.strategy_version,

                /***********************************************************************************
                Documentation helper fields.
                ***********************************************************************************/
                r.readme_storyline_label,
                r.linkedin_post_sequence,
                r.validation_summary_section_hint,

                r.registry_active_flag,

                /***********************************************************************************
                Count active registry rows that share the same technical key.

                Expected:
                    1

                Review:
                    >1 means duplicate active registry mappings exist.
                ***********************************************************************************/
                COUNT(*) OVER (
                    PARTITION BY
                        r.module1_scenario_set_name,
                        r.module1_scenario_name,
                        r.population_id,
                        r.strategy_set_name,
                        r.strategy_name,
                        r.strategy_version
                ) AS registry_match_count,

                /***********************************************************************************
                Deterministic rank used to select one registry row when duplicates exist.

                ORDER BY:
                    run_sequence_number first when available,
                    then module2_run_id for deterministic tie-breaking.
                ***********************************************************************************/
                ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
                    PARTITION BY
                        r.module1_scenario_set_name,
                        r.module1_scenario_name,
                        r.population_id,
                        r.strategy_set_name,
                        r.strategy_name,
                        r.strategy_version
                    ORDER BY
                        r.run_sequence_number NULLS LAST,
                        r.module2_run_id
                ) AS registry_rank

            FROM credit_decisioning_sim.strategy_run_campaign_registry r

            WHERE r.registry_active_flag IS TRUE
        )

        SELECT
            module1_run_id,
            module2_run_id,
            run_sequence_number,

            showcase_id,
            showcase_name,
            comparison_group_id,
            validation_evidence_group_id,

            module1_scenario_set_name,
            module1_scenario_name,
            population_id,

            strategy_set_name,
            strategy_name,
            strategy_version,

            readme_storyline_label,
            linkedin_post_sequence,
            validation_summary_section_hint,

            registry_active_flag,
            registry_match_count,

            CASE
                WHEN registry_match_count = 1
                    THEN 'FRONTIER_REGISTRY_MATCHED'
                ELSE 'FRONTIER_REGISTRY_DUPLICATE_MATCH_REVIEW'
            END AS frontier_registry_match_status

        FROM registry_ranked

        WHERE registry_rank = 1;
    END IF;
END $$;


/*-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
15.0A Review output: campaign registry map available to Section 15.

Business purpose:
    Display registry mappings that can enrich frontier executive outputs.

What to look for:
    For formal campaign documentation, archived frontier rows should ideally map to one active
    registry row.

Review triggers:
    No rows:
        registry table may be unavailable or no active registry rows exist.

    FRONTIER_REGISTRY_DUPLICATE_MATCH_REVIEW:
        more than one active registry row maps to the same technical frontier key.

SQL mechanics:
    This SELECT reads only the temporary map created above.

Boundary:
    Missing rows do not mean missing archive results.
    They mean one or more archive frontier points may not yet have formal campaign IDs.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------*/

SELECT
    *
FROM tmp_m2_strategy_frontier_campaign_registry_map
ORDER BY
    run_sequence_number,
    module2_run_id,
    module1_scenario_set_name,
    module1_scenario_name,
    population_id,
    strategy_set_name,
    strategy_name,
    strategy_version;



/***************************************************************************************************
SECTION 15.1 — ARCHIVED FRONTIER INVENTORY
****************************************************************************************************

PURPOSE:
    Create an inventory of archived strategy / scenario slices available for frontier analysis.

BUSINESS PURPOSE:
    Frontier analysis should start by confirming what archived slices exist before interpreting
    tradeoff metrics.

    This section answers:

        "What completed Module 2 strategy runs are available in the archive, how many rows does each
         contain, and what is the high-level outcome composition for each slice?"

SQL PURPOSE:
    1. Materialize tmp_m2_strategy_frontier_inventory.
    2. Summarize archived row counts by strategy / scenario / population slice.
    3. Confirm distinct application_id counts within each slice.
    4. Surface duplicate application_id counts within each slice.
    5. Show latest-output and archive timestamp ranges.
    6. Show basic final outcome counts.
    7. Show simulated positive offer-exposure count.

WHAT TO LOOK FOR:
    archived_row_count:
        should reflect the completed applicant population for the slice.

    distinct_application_id_count:
        should equal archived_row_count within each slice.

    duplicate_application_row_count:
        should ordinarily be zero.

    approval_count / counteroffer_count / manual_review_count / decline_count:
        provide the first high-level outcome distribution.

    simulated_offer_exposure_count:
        equals APPROVE + COUNTEROFFER if final output conventions are intact.

REVIEW TRIGGERS:
    duplicate_application_row_count > 0:
        Archive grain issue. Frontier outputs should not be interpreted until reviewed.

    Missing baseline slices:
        Not a failure, but baseline-relative deltas will be unavailable for those groups.

    Unexpected row count:
        May indicate incomplete archive persistence, wrong archive reset mode, or a source-scope
        mismatch.

SQL MECHANICS:
    CREATE TEMP TABLE ... AS:
        Materializes the inventory for later diagnostics and review.

    GROUP BY:
        Collapses applicant-level archive rows into one row per strategy / scenario / population
        slice.

    COUNT(*) FILTER:
        Calculates outcome-specific counts in the same grouped query.

GOVERNANCE ROLE:
    Frontier analysis should be archive-driven, not latest-run-driven.

    latest-run output is replaceable.
    archive output is governed strategy history.

BOUNDARY:
    This inventory is read-only against the archive.

    The temporary table is a diagnostic helper only.

***************************************************************************************************/

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS tmp_m2_strategy_frontier_inventory;

CREATE TEMP TABLE tmp_m2_strategy_frontier_inventory
ON COMMIT PRESERVE ROWS
AS
SELECT
    /***********************************************************************************************
    Technical frontier key.

    This is the core grain for Section 15 summary outputs.
    ***********************************************************************************************/
    strategy_set_name,
    strategy_name,
    strategy_version,

    module1_scenario_set_name,
    module1_scenario_name,
    population_id,

    /***********************************************************************************************
    Row-count and grain diagnostics.

    Expected within each archived slice:
        archived_row_count = distinct_application_id_count
        duplicate_application_row_count = 0
    ***********************************************************************************************/
    COUNT(*) AS archived_row_count,
    COUNT(DISTINCT application_id) AS distinct_application_id_count,

    COUNT(*) - COUNT(DISTINCT application_id) AS duplicate_application_row_count,

    /***********************************************************************************************
    Latest-run and archive timestamp ranges.

    These are audit metadata only.
    They are not comparison keys and not frontier ranking criteria.
    ***********************************************************************************************/
    MIN(latest_output_created_ts) AS min_latest_output_created_ts,
    MAX(latest_output_created_ts) AS max_latest_output_created_ts,

    MIN(archive_inserted_ts) AS min_archive_inserted_ts,
    MAX(archive_inserted_ts) AS max_archive_inserted_ts,

    /***********************************************************************************************
    Final outcome counts.

    These provide a quick outcome composition view before detailed frontier metrics are calculated.
    ***********************************************************************************************/
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE decision_outcome = 'APPROVE') AS approval_count,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE decision_outcome = 'COUNTEROFFER') AS counteroffer_count,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE decision_outcome = 'MANUAL_REVIEW') AS manual_review_count,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE decision_outcome = 'DECLINE') AS decline_count,

    /***********************************************************************************************
    Simulated positive offer-exposure count.

    Expected:
        APPROVE + COUNTEROFFER.
    ***********************************************************************************************/
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE simulated_offer_exposure_flag IS TRUE)
        AS simulated_offer_exposure_count

FROM credit_decisioning_sim.strategy_decisions_archive

GROUP BY
    strategy_set_name,
    strategy_name,
    strategy_version,
    module1_scenario_set_name,
    module1_scenario_name,
    population_id;

/***************************************************************************************************
SECTION 15.2 — STRATEGY FRONTIER SUMMARY
****************************************************************************************************

PURPOSE:
    Produce one summary row per archived Module 1 scenario × Module 2 strategy slice.

BUSINESS PURPOSE:
    Create the core frontier summary table that converts archived applicant-level strategy outputs
    into portfolio-level strategy tradeoff metrics.

    This section answers:

        "For each archived strategy / scenario slice, what are the core access, exposure, risk,
         affordability, Expected Loss, and reason-code characteristics?"

SQL PURPOSE:
    1. Materialize tmp_m2_strategy_frontier_summary.
    2. Calculate final decision counts and rates.
    3. Calculate simulated positive offer-exposure counts and rates.
    4. Calculate approval and counteroffer shares among offer rows.
    5. Calculate requested amount and approved amount totals / averages.
    6. Calculate counteroffer exposure-reduction averages.
    7. Calculate requested PTI and approved PTI averages.
    8. Calculate synthetic estimated-risk proxy averages across all rows, offer rows, declined rows,
       and manual-review rows.
    9. Calculate LGD averages.
    10. Calculate requested Expected Loss and approved Expected Loss metrics.
    11. Calculate requested and approved Expected Loss rates.
    12. Identify top primary reason code.
    13. Identify top non-approval reason code.
    14. Identify top policy-stop reason code.

BUSINESS INTERPRETATION:
    This is the core strategy frontier table.

    It summarizes:
        decision distribution,
        simulated offer exposure,
        approved amount,
        approved affordability,
        synthetic estimated-risk profile,
        requested Expected Loss,
        approved Expected Loss,
        approved Expected Loss rate,
        and primary reason-code concentration.

WHAT TO LOOK FOR:
    simulated_offer_exposure_rate:
        access / positive simulated offer exposure.

    total_approved_amount:
        simulated approved exposure impact.

    total_approved_expected_loss_amount:
        total synthetic approved-exposure Expected Loss.

    approved_expected_loss_rate:
        approved Expected Loss per approved exposure dollar.

    counteroffer_share_of_offers:
        reliance on reduced-exposure treatment among positive offer rows.

    manual_review_rate:
        unresolved outcome burden.

    decline_rate:
        no-offer concentration.

    top_non_approval_primary_reason_code:
        most useful executive explanation when top_primary_reason_code is simply APPROVED_AS_REQUESTED.

REVIEW TRIGGERS:
    High approved Expected Loss rate:
        review risk, product, LGD, approved amount, and strategy posture.

    High counteroffer share:
        review whether strategy depends heavily on reduced-exposure treatment.

    High manual-review rate:
        review unresolved operational burden.

    Dominant policy-stop reason:
        review whether no-offer concentration aligns to strategy intent.

METRIC CONVENTIONS:
    approval_rate:
        approval_count / applications

    counteroffer_rate:
        counteroffer_count / applications

    manual_review_rate:
        manual_review_count / applications

    decline_rate:
        decline_count / applications

    simulated_offer_exposure_rate:
        simulated_offer_exposure_count / applications

    approval_share_of_offers:
        approval_count / simulated_offer_exposure_count

    counteroffer_share_of_offers:
        counteroffer_count / simulated_offer_exposure_count

    requested_expected_loss_rate:
        total_requested_expected_loss_amount / total_requested_amount

    approved_expected_loss_rate:
        total_approved_expected_loss_amount / total_approved_amount

    All-application approved exposure metrics:
        Use COALESCE(approved_amount, 0)
        Use COALESCE(approved_expected_loss_amount, 0)

    Offer-row metrics:
        Use FILTER (WHERE simulated_offer_exposure_flag IS TRUE)

WHY NON-APPROVAL REASON FIELDS ARE INCLUDED:
    top_primary_reason_code is often APPROVED_AS_REQUESTED.

    That is technically correct but not always the most useful executive explanation of strategy
    movement.

    top_non_approval_primary_reason_code and top_policy_stop_primary_reason_code help explain what
    constrains access, drives reduced exposure, or concentrates final no-offer outcomes.

SQL MECHANICS:
    slice_summary:
        Collapses archived applicant rows into one summary row per frontier key.

    reason_counts:
        Counts primary reason-code distribution and ranks reason codes within each slice.

    non_approval_reason_counts:
        Identifies the most common non-approval reason code.

    policy_stop_reason_counts:
        Identifies the most common policy-stop reason code.

    LEFT JOIN:
        Adds reason-code story fields without dropping frontier rows if a particular reason family is
        absent.

BOUNDARY:
    approved_expected_loss_rate is a synthetic strategy frontier metric.

    It is not a production loss-rate forecast.
    It is not profitability.
    It is not capital consumption.
    It is not risk-adjusted margin.

***************************************************************************************************/

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS tmp_m2_strategy_frontier_summary;

CREATE TEMP TABLE tmp_m2_strategy_frontier_summary
ON COMMIT PRESERVE ROWS
AS
WITH slice_summary AS (
    SELECT
        /*******************************************************************************************
        Frontier grain:
            one archived strategy / Module 1 scenario / population slice.
        *******************************************************************************************/
        strategy_set_name,
        strategy_name,
        strategy_version,

        module1_scenario_set_name,
        module1_scenario_name,
        population_id,

        /*******************************************************************************************
        Population size.
        *******************************************************************************************/
        COUNT(*) AS applications,

        /*******************************************************************************************
        Final outcome counts.
        *******************************************************************************************/
        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE decision_outcome = 'APPROVE') AS approval_count,
        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE decision_outcome = 'COUNTEROFFER') AS counteroffer_count,
        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE decision_outcome = 'MANUAL_REVIEW') AS manual_review_count,
        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE decision_outcome = 'DECLINE') AS decline_count,

        /*******************************************************************************************
        Positive simulated offer-exposure count.

        TRUE for APPROVE and COUNTEROFFER only.
        *******************************************************************************************/
        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE simulated_offer_exposure_flag IS TRUE)
            AS simulated_offer_exposure_count,

        /*******************************************************************************************
        Final decision rates.

        SQL mechanics:
            FILTER counts the outcome-specific numerator.
            COUNT(*) is the archived-slice denominator.
            NULLIF prevents divide-by-zero.
        *******************************************************************************************/
        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE decision_outcome = 'APPROVE')::NUMERIC
            / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS approval_rate,

        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE decision_outcome = 'COUNTEROFFER')::NUMERIC
            / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS counteroffer_rate,

        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE decision_outcome = 'MANUAL_REVIEW')::NUMERIC
            / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS manual_review_rate,

        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE decision_outcome = 'DECLINE')::NUMERIC
            / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS decline_rate,

        /*******************************************************************************************
        Positive simulated offer-exposure rate.

        Use this as the high-level access / positive-offer metric.
        *******************************************************************************************/
        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE simulated_offer_exposure_flag IS TRUE)::NUMERIC
            / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS simulated_offer_exposure_rate,

        /*******************************************************************************************
        Offer composition.

        approval_share_of_offers:
            share of positive offer rows that were final APPROVE.

        counteroffer_share_of_offers:
            share of positive offer rows that were final COUNTEROFFER.
        *******************************************************************************************/
        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE decision_outcome = 'APPROVE')::NUMERIC
            / NULLIF(COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE simulated_offer_exposure_flag IS TRUE), 0)
            AS approval_share_of_offers,

        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE decision_outcome = 'COUNTEROFFER')::NUMERIC
            / NULLIF(COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE simulated_offer_exposure_flag IS TRUE), 0)
            AS counteroffer_share_of_offers,

        /*******************************************************************************************
        Requested and approved exposure totals.

        COALESCE turns unresolved / no-offer approved exposure into zero for portfolio-impact
        metrics.
        *******************************************************************************************/
        SUM(requested_amount) AS total_requested_amount,
        SUM(COALESCE(approved_amount, 0)) AS total_approved_amount,

        AVG(requested_amount) AS avg_requested_amount,
        AVG(COALESCE(approved_amount, 0)) AS avg_approved_amount_all_apps,

        /*******************************************************************************************
        Offer-row approved amount.

        FILTER keeps this metric focused on final APPROVE and COUNTEROFFER rows.
        *******************************************************************************************/
        AVG(approved_amount) FILTER (WHERE simulated_offer_exposure_flag IS TRUE)
            AS avg_approved_amount_offer_rows,

        /*******************************************************************************************
        Counteroffer exposure reduction.

        Populated only for final COUNTEROFFER rows.
        *******************************************************************************************/
        AVG(exposure_reduction_pct) FILTER (WHERE decision_outcome = 'COUNTEROFFER')
            AS avg_exposure_reduction_pct_counteroffers,

        /*******************************************************************************************
        Requested and approved affordability.

        requested_payment_to_income_ratio:
            original requested-structure PTI.

        approved_payment_to_income_ratio:
            final approved-exposure PTI proxy for offer rows.
        *******************************************************************************************/
        AVG(requested_payment_to_income_ratio)
            AS avg_requested_payment_to_income_ratio,

        AVG(approved_payment_to_income_ratio) FILTER (WHERE simulated_offer_exposure_flag IS TRUE)
            AS avg_approved_payment_to_income_ratio_offer_rows,

        /*******************************************************************************************
        Synthetic estimated-risk profile.

        estimated_pd remains the SQL field name and is interpreted as synthetic estimated-PD proxy.
        *******************************************************************************************/
        AVG(estimated_pd) AS avg_synthetic_estimated_pd_proxy_all_apps,

        AVG(estimated_pd) FILTER (WHERE simulated_offer_exposure_flag IS TRUE)
            AS avg_synthetic_estimated_pd_proxy_offer_rows,

        AVG(estimated_pd) FILTER (WHERE decision_outcome = 'DECLINE')
            AS avg_synthetic_estimated_pd_proxy_declined_rows,

        AVG(estimated_pd) FILTER (WHERE decision_outcome = 'MANUAL_REVIEW')
            AS avg_synthetic_estimated_pd_proxy_manual_review_rows,

        /*******************************************************************************************
        LGD profile.

        LGD remains a Module 1 risk-severity approximation.
        *******************************************************************************************/
        AVG(estimated_lgd) AS avg_estimated_lgd_all_apps,

        AVG(estimated_lgd) FILTER (WHERE simulated_offer_exposure_flag IS TRUE)
            AS avg_estimated_lgd_offer_rows,

        /*******************************************************************************************
        Requested and approved Expected Loss totals and averages.

        requested_expected_loss_amount:
            requested-exposure Expected Loss.

        approved_expected_loss_amount:
            approved-exposure Expected Loss after final Module 2 exposure treatment.
        *******************************************************************************************/
        SUM(requested_expected_loss_amount) AS total_requested_expected_loss_amount,

        SUM(COALESCE(approved_expected_loss_amount, 0))
            AS total_approved_expected_loss_amount,

        AVG(requested_expected_loss_amount) AS avg_requested_expected_loss_amount,

        AVG(COALESCE(approved_expected_loss_amount, 0))
            AS avg_approved_expected_loss_all_apps,

        AVG(approved_expected_loss_amount) FILTER (WHERE simulated_offer_exposure_flag IS TRUE)
            AS avg_approved_expected_loss_offer_rows,

        /*******************************************************************************************
        Expected Loss rates.

        requested_expected_loss_rate:
            requested EL / requested amount.

        approved_expected_loss_rate:
            approved EL / approved amount.

        Boundary:
            These are synthetic strategy metrics, not production loss-rate forecasts.
        *******************************************************************************************/
        SUM(requested_expected_loss_amount)
            / NULLIF(SUM(requested_amount), 0)
            AS requested_expected_loss_rate,

        SUM(COALESCE(approved_expected_loss_amount, 0))
            / NULLIF(SUM(COALESCE(approved_amount, 0)), 0)
            AS approved_expected_loss_rate

    FROM credit_decisioning_sim.strategy_decisions_archive

    GROUP BY
        strategy_set_name,
        strategy_name,
        strategy_version,
        module1_scenario_set_name,
        module1_scenario_name,
        population_id
),

reason_counts AS (
    /***********************************************************************************************
    CTE: reason_counts

    Purpose:
        Rank primary reason codes within each archived strategy / scenario slice.

    SQL mechanics:
        COUNT(*) creates reason-code frequency.
        Window SUM creates the population-share denominator.
        ROW_NUMBER selects the top reason code deterministically.

    Interpretation:
        top_primary_reason_code is often APPROVED_AS_REQUESTED for high-approval strategies.
    ***********************************************************************************************/
    SELECT
        strategy_set_name,
        strategy_name,
        strategy_version,

        module1_scenario_set_name,
        module1_scenario_name,
        population_id,

        primary_reason_family,
        primary_reason_code,

        COUNT(*) AS primary_reason_row_count,

        COUNT(*)::NUMERIC
            / NULLIF(
                SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (
                    PARTITION BY
                        strategy_set_name,
                        strategy_name,
                        strategy_version,
                        module1_scenario_set_name,
                        module1_scenario_name,
                        population_id
                ),
                0
            ) AS primary_reason_population_share,

        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY
                strategy_set_name,
                strategy_name,
                strategy_version,
                module1_scenario_set_name,
                module1_scenario_name,
                population_id
            ORDER BY
                COUNT(*) DESC,
                primary_reason_family,
                primary_reason_code
        ) AS reason_rank

    FROM credit_decisioning_sim.strategy_decisions_archive

    GROUP BY
        strategy_set_name,
        strategy_name,
        strategy_version,
        module1_scenario_set_name,
        module1_scenario_name,
        population_id,
        primary_reason_family,
        primary_reason_code
),

non_approval_reason_counts AS (
    /***********************************************************************************************
    CTE: non_approval_reason_counts

    Purpose:
        Identify the top non-approval reason code.

    Why this matters:
        APPROVED_AS_REQUESTED may dominate top_primary_reason_code, but executive storytelling often
        needs the most common constraint or non-approval driver.
    ***********************************************************************************************/
    SELECT
        strategy_set_name,
        strategy_name,
        strategy_version,

        module1_scenario_set_name,
        module1_scenario_name,
        population_id,

        primary_reason_family,
        primary_reason_code,

        COUNT(*) AS non_approval_reason_row_count,

        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY
                strategy_set_name,
                strategy_name,
                strategy_version,
                module1_scenario_set_name,
                module1_scenario_name,
                population_id
            ORDER BY
                COUNT(*) DESC,
                primary_reason_family,
                primary_reason_code
        ) AS non_approval_reason_rank

    FROM credit_decisioning_sim.strategy_decisions_archive

    WHERE decision_outcome <> 'APPROVE'

    GROUP BY
        strategy_set_name,
        strategy_name,
        strategy_version,
        module1_scenario_set_name,
        module1_scenario_name,
        population_id,
        primary_reason_family,
        primary_reason_code
),

policy_stop_reason_counts AS (
    /***********************************************************************************************
    CTE: policy_stop_reason_counts

    Purpose:
        Identify the top policy-stop reason code.

    Why this matters:
        Policy-stop concentration helps explain final no-offer behavior.

    Boundary:
        POLICY_STOP reason codes are simulated strategy explanation codes, not adverse-action
        reasons or customer communication text.
    ***********************************************************************************************/
    SELECT
        strategy_set_name,
        strategy_name,
        strategy_version,

        module1_scenario_set_name,
        module1_scenario_name,
        population_id,

        primary_reason_family,
        primary_reason_code,

        COUNT(*) AS policy_stop_reason_row_count,

        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY
                strategy_set_name,
                strategy_name,
                strategy_version,
                module1_scenario_set_name,
                module1_scenario_name,
                population_id
            ORDER BY
                COUNT(*) DESC,
                primary_reason_family,
                primary_reason_code
        ) AS policy_stop_reason_rank

    FROM credit_decisioning_sim.strategy_decisions_archive

    WHERE primary_reason_family = 'POLICY_STOP'

    GROUP BY
        strategy_set_name,
        strategy_name,
        strategy_version,
        module1_scenario_set_name,
        module1_scenario_name,
        population_id,
        primary_reason_family,
        primary_reason_code
)

SELECT
    /***********************************************************************************************
    Carry all core frontier metrics from the slice summary.
    ***********************************************************************************************/
    s.*,

    /***********************************************************************************************
    Top primary reason code overall.
    ***********************************************************************************************/
    r.primary_reason_family AS top_primary_reason_family,
    r.primary_reason_code AS top_primary_reason_code,
    r.primary_reason_row_count AS top_primary_reason_row_count,
    r.primary_reason_population_share AS top_primary_reason_population_share,

    /***********************************************************************************************
    Storytelling enhancement:
        top_primary_reason_code is often APPROVED_AS_REQUESTED, which is technically correct but not
        always the most useful executive explanation of strategy movement.

        The top non-approval reason fields identify the most common non-approval simulated strategy
        explanation code within the archived strategy slice.

        The top policy-stop reason fields isolate the dominant simulated no-offer explanation code.

        These fields support frontier interpretation without changing any decision, exposure,
        Expected Loss, archive, or reason-code assignment logic.
    ***********************************************************************************************/
    nr.primary_reason_family AS top_non_approval_primary_reason_family,
    nr.primary_reason_code AS top_non_approval_primary_reason_code,

    nr.non_approval_reason_row_count::NUMERIC
        / NULLIF(s.applications, 0) AS top_non_approval_reason_population_share,

    ps.primary_reason_family AS top_policy_stop_primary_reason_family,
    ps.primary_reason_code AS top_policy_stop_primary_reason_code,

    ps.policy_stop_reason_row_count::NUMERIC
        / NULLIF(s.applications, 0) AS top_policy_stop_reason_population_share

FROM slice_summary s

LEFT JOIN reason_counts r
    ON r.strategy_set_name = s.strategy_set_name
   AND r.strategy_name = s.strategy_name
   AND r.strategy_version = s.strategy_version
   AND r.module1_scenario_set_name = s.module1_scenario_set_name
   AND r.module1_scenario_name = s.module1_scenario_name
   AND r.population_id = s.population_id
   AND r.reason_rank = 1

LEFT JOIN non_approval_reason_counts nr
    ON nr.strategy_set_name = s.strategy_set_name
   AND nr.strategy_name = s.strategy_name
   AND nr.strategy_version = s.strategy_version
   AND nr.module1_scenario_set_name = s.module1_scenario_set_name
   AND nr.module1_scenario_name = s.module1_scenario_name
   AND nr.population_id = s.population_id
   AND nr.non_approval_reason_rank = 1

LEFT JOIN policy_stop_reason_counts ps
    ON ps.strategy_set_name = s.strategy_set_name
   AND ps.strategy_name = s.strategy_name
   AND ps.strategy_version = s.strategy_version
   AND ps.module1_scenario_set_name = s.module1_scenario_set_name
   AND ps.module1_scenario_name = s.module1_scenario_name
   AND ps.population_id = s.population_id
   AND ps.policy_stop_reason_rank = 1;
